item.title: Miller Lite ‘Clinch Cans’ commemorate Milwaukee Brewers World Series win
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are celebrating the team’s first World Series championship in grand style in Tampa Bay. Back in Milwaukee, Miller is packaging special “Clinch Cans” of Miller Lite from the beer being produced on the line at precisely 10:13 PM CDT when the team recorded the final out of Game 5 and officially became World Series Champions. 4,400 “Clinch Cans” will be available online beginning November 2. The quantity selected is likely related to the 44 years that have passed since the Brewers last World Series appearance in 1982. MORE: Brewers win 2026 World Series: Now only 4 franchises remain without title A collector’s item Milwaukee Brewers center fielder Garrett Mitchell (5) and Milwaukee Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt (12) celebrate Pratt’s home run against the Tampa Bay Rays during the twelfth inning during Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Oct 27, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Clinch Cans will look nothing like the traditional white Miller Lite can with the word Lite in blue. JUST IN: Miller Lite says it took beer that was on the line at 10:13 pm CT, when the Brewers won it all, and put it special "Clinch Cans." 4,400 cans will be available online starting 11/2. https://t.co/ZsllSOtE1r — Darren Rovell (@darrenrovell) October 29, 2026 They will have the Brewers colors of blue and yellow, with the Brewers logo, and the stitching printed like that on a baseball. The word Lite will be printed in yellow. Near the bottom of the can, also in yellow, the phrase “Clinched 2026” will appear. Given how quickly the Brewers World Series merchandise flew off shelves , these cans will be snapped up quickly. MORE: Brewers’ Christian Yelich sends message to Milwaukee, Bob Uecker Milwaukee and MLB fans should enjoy this Many MLB fans wanted the World Series to last longer so that we had baseball for longer. Amid the Brewers much-deserved win and celebrations is plenty of uncertainty about what the future holds. Barring a miracle, a lockout will happen on December 2. Some fear there will be limited or worse yet no baseball in 2027. And just like that, we have no idea when we'll see a live MLB game next — Depressed Phillies Fan (@mlb_phanatic) October 29, 2026 Watching the joy on the Brewers players’ faces and juxtapositioning it with the doom and gloom of a lockout trigger unsettling emotions. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Understanding Brian Flores’ Blitz-Heavy Scheme
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Eric Wilson #55 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates with Blake Cashman #51 against the Indianapolis Colts during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings under defensive coordinator Brian Flores run a unique scheme that has become a hot topic around the league after dominating every opponent en route to a 6-0 start for the Vikings. It is a blitz-heavy scheme but it’s not about simply dialing up pressure and hoping not to get burned. It’s Not Just About Rushing the Passer The first thing to know about Flores’ blitz-heavy scheme is it’s not just about rushing the passer, it’s a total defensive philosophy designed to stop the run and pass, dictate the terms of engagement, and make execution for the offense more difficult- forcing mistakes. There are several intertwined elements to what is really a unique scheme in the NFL at the moment, which is rare. Foundational Elements and Principles The foundation of Brian Flores’ scheme is a five (or more) man front paired with a secondary playing zone coverage. That is what you are likely to see on around 80% of the Vikings’ defensive plays. A 5+ Man Attacking Front The defensive front operates an attacking, aggressive style, with defensive linemen penetrating gaps and linebackers blitzing and twisting. This contrasts with other schemes where defensive linemen are tasked with defending a gap-and-a-half or two gaps by catching blocks or taking on double-teams to keep linebackers clean. Edge rushers are tasked with setting edges, rushing the passer, or dropping into coverage. Beyond that, Flores will often place or walk-up other defenders to the line of scrimmage, either bringing or simulating additional pressure. The key in all of this is to pressure the quarterback and offense both physically and mentally- and not just occasionally but every down. Zone Coverage On the back end, the Vikings play a variety of zone coverages, frequently disguised pre-snap, and also man coverage on rare occasions. This contrasts with the man coverage that has typically accompanied blitzing fronts in the past. One key here is that the zone shell coverage is better able to prevent or limit the explosive plays that can result when a blitz doesn’t get home in time. The other key is that the coverages vary and can be difficult (or impossible) for a quarterback to differentiate pre-snap and often early post-snap as well. Numbers, Angles, Matchups- and Chaos The object of every football play or scheme is to create advantages in numbers (players), angles, and/or matchups. Brian Flores’ scheme is no different in that regard. But the high blitz rate on every down and the variability of blitz packages and coverages adds a degree or two of difficulty for opposing quarterbacks and offenses to deal with that can wear them down mentally as well as physically over the course of

item.title: Wisconsin's Adaline Sheplee has efficient performance in exhibition win | Takeaways
item.description: MADISON – Eight was enough for the Wisconsin women’s basketball team Oct. 28. The Badgers scored a 101-69 victory over Wisconsin -Eau Claire in their only exhibition of the preseason with just eight players due to injuries and Illness. All eight Badgers played at least 20 minutes. Six scored in double figures and six had at least two assists. Freshman Adaline Sheplee scored 25 points on 8-for-10 shooting. Iowa transfer Teagan Mallegni added 17 points, hitting six of eight shots overall and five of seven from 3-point range. The Badgers played without six players: freshman Giselle Janowski, sophomores Dorja Zaja and Alba Martin Mesa, senior Kyrah Daniels and fifth-years Kadidia Toure and Shay Bollin. Janowski, Zaja, Martin Mesa, Daniels and Toure sat out a practice Oct. 26 that was open to the media. After the exhibition, Badgers coach Robin Pingeton didn’t name names but noted that an illness recently hit the team. “We didn't realize going into the day that we were only going to have eight but just had a little sickness that popped up last night,” Pingeton said. “So different rotations, people playing different positions, but I thought they really did a good job of embracing that part of it for sure." Here are three takeaways from the contests. Plenty of teaching points for the defense Wisconsin played aggressive on the ball defense, which resulted in many of its 15 steals. The players also hit the floor and hustled for loose balls. Overall, however, the execution defensively wasn’t up to Pingeton's expectations. Eau Claire, which is learning the system of a new coach, was shooting 53% (23 of 43) through three quarters though it trailed, 78-61. The Blugolds cut and passed their way to 15 layups and 23 layup attempts. They scored 34 points in the paint. “I think part of the problem is we just thought we could be so aggressive and physical and blow things up,” Pingeton said. “(Eau Claire) did a really good job playing with pace and really nailing their screens and we'd get caught and we'd trail and then we didn't give each other notifications, we didn't switch when we needed to.” Credit UW for a much better fourth quarter. Pingeton challenged the team to hold Eau Claire to no more than 10 points and delivered. The Blugolds scored eight points, just two in the paint, and shot 21.4% (3 for 14). Adaline Sheplee does damage in the paint The pathway to a 25-point night for Sheplee ran through the paint. The 6-foot-3 guard hit two 3s but used her ball-handling and size to get in paint and get high-percentage looks. Five of her buckets came from about 5 feet. Due to the team’s injuries and Illiness, Sheplee also played some center, a role she had not played much in practice. “I knew that there was an opportunity for me to get minutes with having eight players and so I came in with the mentality that I want to prove myself and utilize my versatility against this team,” Sheplee said. “I'm happy with certain areas, and there's a lot of other areas I know I ne

item.title: Brewers’ William Contreras, Pat Murphy share incredible moment after World Series win
item.description: Mark Hoffman/Milwaukee Journal Sentinel Brewers’ William Contreras, Pat Murphy share incredible moment after World Series win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers have done it. In the franchise’s 58th year of existence, they can finally call themselves World Series champion after taking down the Tampa Bay Rays, 4-1, in Game 5 of the 2026 edition of the Fall Classic. The Brewers waited 44 years for an opportunity to redeem themselves after losing in their first and only other World Series appearance, and as the old adage goes, patience may be bitter but its fruits are sweet. Just to show how sweet it must feel for the entire Brewers team to have finally gotten over the hump, the moment star catcher William Contreras and manager Pat Murphy shared after they closed out the Rays in Game 5 says it all . Via Enrique Rojas of ESPN: Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) William Contreras y manager Pat Murphy. Eso es todo, amigos. pic.twitter.com/jyJDeuQ9i0 — Enrique Rojas/ESPN (@Enrique_Rojas1) October 29, 2026 Contreras has experienced quite a few postseason heartbreaks with the Brewers, having been part of the team’s core since 2023. He saw Milwaukee come up short in the Wild Card round in two consecutive postseasons, and then he was there to witness his team get swept by the Los Angeles Dodgers in the 2025 NLCS. But the Brewers, despite the changes their roster have gone through year after year, have stayed the course. Contreras has been a bastion of consistency , and he has relished being the leader of this elite ballclub. He is the extension of Murphy when he’s out there calling pitches and organizing his team, and now they can call themselves champion. Meanwhile, Murphy knows how to push his team’s buttons, getting the best out of them on every single turn. It’s incredible how the Brewers didn’t necessarily expect that he’ll have to take over as manager, but after Craig Counsell left rather unceremoniously , Murphy kept this team humming and not skipping a single beat. The Brewers wouldn’t be here if it weren’t for Contreras and Murphy, and they deserve all the celebrations they’ll be doing over the next few weeks as they have immortalized themselves in MLB lore. Related: Bucks join Brewers World Series party with five-word post Related: Brewers’ Aaron Ashby caps 2026 postseason with bonkers ERA

item.title: Shane Van Gisbergen Has Changed NASCAR, But The Sport Still Needs To Prove He Can Win Anywhere
item.description: Jun 28, 2026; Sonoma, California, USA; Trackhouse Racing driver Shane Van Gisbergen (97) celebrates after winning the NASCAR Toyota / Save Mart 350 series race at Sonoma Raceway. Mandatory Credit: Stan Szeto-Imagn Images Shane van Gisbergen has already proved that his road-course talent translates to NASCAR. The next question is how quickly he can become a threat everywhere. The Trackhouse Racing driver has changed expectations for international talent entering American stock-car racing. His road-course ability is exceptional, and his presence has added another compelling storyline to the Cup Series. But NASCAR is not a road-course championship. The Oval Question Still Matters Martinsville demands a different skill set. Drivers need patience in traffic, strong braking, tire management and the ability to handle repeated contact without losing their rhythm. It is not enough to be spectacular on a circuit with right turns. SVG’s supporters can reasonably argue that his overall development has been impressive. His critics can also point out that success across the full schedule is the standard for a Cup Series contender. Both things can be true. What Would Make SVG A True Championship Threat? The next step is consistency across every type of track. Winning on road courses establishes credibility, but competing for a championship requires collecting strong results on ovals, short tracks and superspeedways, too. That is a difficult transition, even for talented drivers. Van Gisbergen has the opportunity to silence more doubters as he gains experience. But the sport should not crown him an all-around master before he proves it over a full championship campaign. The potential is obvious. The challenge is proving that potential everywhere. And that is what makes his NASCAR journey worth watching.

item.title: NASCAR’s Martinsville Playoff Race Could Get Ugly Fast, And That Is Exactly What The Sport Needs
item.description: Photo by: Jim Dedmon If you want clean air, polite racing and 37 drivers staying out of each other’s way, Martinsville might not be your favorite Sunday afternoon. Good. NASCAR heads to the paperclip this weekend for a race with championship implications and almost no room for error. Kyle Larson enters with a massive points lead, while Denny Hamlin and Christopher Bell need extraordinary weekends to stay alive. The pressure should make every restart fascinating. Martinsville Is Supposed To Be Difficult Martinsville is not a track where drivers can casually cruise through traffic. The tight corners, short straightaways and heavy braking create opportunities for contact. That is part of the appeal. Fans complain when races become processional. Then they complain when drivers get aggressive enough to change the outcome. NASCAR cannot have it both ways. Short-track racing involves risk, and playoff pressure only increases the intensity. There is a difference between deliberate wrecking and hard racing. But Martinsville has a way of putting that distinction to the test. The Championship Could Turn On One Moment Larson has the points advantage, but Martinsville still demands a complete performance. A bad pit stop, damaged car or poorly timed incident could change the weekend. For the drivers chasing him, playing it safe may not be enough. That creates the kind of tension NASCAR needs during the championship fight. The sport should want drivers fighting for every position, not protecting themselves from criticism. If Martinsville delivers a wild finish, expect complaints. Also expect everyone to watch. Sometimes the best NASCAR races are the ones that leave the garage arguing long after the checkered flag.

item.title: Brewers set World Series celebration for Friday, October 30
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 22: World Series signage is seen during a workout day prior to game on of the 2026 World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on October 22, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images After capturing the franchise’s first World Series title on Wednesday night in Tampa Bay, the Milwaukee Brewers are set to return to Milwaukee to celebrate with the city and state at a parade on Friday, October 30. The championship marked the culmination of a historic season that featured the team’s first appearance in the World Series since 1982. It featured packed watch parties and sold-out crowds with unforgettable moments along the way. Brewers fans across Wisconsin and beyond helped fuel the most memorable chapter in franchise history. Together, players, coaches, staff, alumni, and fans have brought a World Series championship home to Milwaukee. The Milwaukee Brewers Championship Celebration will feature a parade through the heart of the city on historic Wisconsin Avenue, as well as a rally and fan festival to bring the community together to honor the World Series champions. The parade is set to begin at 10 a.m. at the intersection of North 4th Street and West Wisconsin Avenue, proceeding through downtown Milwaukee before concluding at Henry Maier Festival Park, where a rally will take place throughout the grounds. Admission to the festival grounds will be free to all fans until capacity is reached. Tickets for the American Family Insurance Amphitheater for the rally speeches will be available on Thursday, October 29 with staggered season seat member presales starting at 10 a.m. and public tickets on sale at 2 p.m. Net proceeds will benefit the Brewers Community Foundation. For fans without tickets, the rally speeches will be available on various video boards throughout the festival grounds. The grounds will open to the public at 8 a.m. to accommodate fans. On the grounds, guests can enjoy multiple viewing locations with large video screens featuring live parade coverage, along with live music and a variety of food and beverage offerings. For festival park entry and venue policies, visit AmFamAmp.com . Fans will also have the opportunity to purchase exclusive Brewers parade/rally merchandise during the celebration at Henry Maier Festival Park. The first 50,000 fans at the rally will also receive a limited-edition championship rally towel. The Brewers Team Store at American Family Field will open at 9 a.m. on Thursday, October 29, and will operate exclusively out of the merchandise tent located in the 3rd base plaza. To learn more about the celebration, fans should visit brewers.com/parade and follow the Brewers’ official social media channels for any additional updates.

item.title: Denny Hamlin Is Running Out Of Excuses, And Martinsville Could Decide His NASCAR Legacy
item.description: Oct 25, 2025; Martinsville, Virginia, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Denny Hamlin (11) before NASCAR Cup Series Xfinity 500 Qualifying at Martinsville Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Denny Hamlin has spent years being one of NASCAR’s best drivers without winning the Cup Series championship. Now, his latest title opportunity is hanging by a thread. Hamlin trails Kyle Larson by 73 points entering Martinsville. He needs an enormous weekend to keep his championship hopes alive. For a driver with Hamlin’s experience and equipment, that is a brutal position. The Window Is Closing Hamlin has the talent to win races. He has the team, the experience and the short-track credentials to make a serious run at Martinsville. But his 2026 postseason has been plagued by problems. Incidents, bad finishes and missed opportunities have left him chasing Larson instead of controlling the championship. At some point, the excuses stop mattering. Championships are not awarded for having a fast car or being competitive for most of the year. Drivers have to deliver when the stakes are highest. Can Hamlin Finally Change The Narrative? Martinsville gives Hamlin an opportunity to fight back. It is also a reminder of how difficult his championship mission has become. If Larson outscores him by three or more points Sunday, Hamlin’s title hopes are over. That leaves little room for another mistake. Hamlin has accomplished plenty in NASCAR, and a championship would not erase the success he has already enjoyed. But the missing title remains the obvious question surrounding his career. Is this finally the year he gets it done, or will NASCAR fans spend another offseason debating what might have been? Sunday could provide the answer.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham gives Caitlin Clark reason Indiana went from WNBA ‘nap town’ to people’s ‘Super Bowl’
item.description: Photo by Tara Walton/Getty Images In a recent podcast appearance talking to Theo Von, Sophie Cunningham explained how much the Indiana Fever’s status has changed in recent years. The Indiana Fever have been the WNBA’s most-watched franchise since they drafted Caitlin Clark. Their fame went to another level this season, even as Sophie Cunningham emerged as one of the league’s most popular figures. The team wasn’t able to go deep in the playoffs, but they remain quite loved. This wasn’t always the case. The Fever won a championship in 2012 and were decently successful in the Tamika Catchings era, but they struggled a lot after 2016. The two years before drafting Clark were arguably the franchise’s worst, and Cunningham recently noted the change she herself has witnessed. Sophie Cunningham admits Indiana Fever’s support and popularity increased dramatically during her own career Cunningham was drafted by the Phoenix Mercury in 2019 and has been in the WNBA since. The 30-year-old has been in Indiana since 2025, although there has been a lot of speculation on whether she will remain with the team moving forward. In any case, she spoke on a recent podcast about how much things have changed for the franchise since the arrival of Caitlin Clark and the other superstars from her draft class. “When I got drafted, Indiana, I think they only had like 200 fans,” Cunningham said. “Like, it was a nap town. People went there to catch up on sleep. You played a game and you wanted to get out. Now, that’s the place you want to play. That’s like people’s Super Bowl… Now, every arena’s like that.” The 2024 WNBA draft changed a lot of things around the league. Their popularity is now at an all-time high, especially the Fever. While they still do have a lot of growing to do, the past couple of years have been immense for women’s basketball overall. item.title: NASCAR Fans Better Appreciate Kyle Larson Now, Because Another Championship Could Make This Era Look Ridiculous
item.description: Sep 2, 2026; Charlotte, NC, USA; Kyle Larson answers questions from the media during the Chase media day at the Charlotte Convention Center. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Kyle Larson is approaching a milestone that should make every NASCAR fan pay attention. The defending Cup Series champion enters Martinsville with a 73-point advantage over Denny Hamlin. He can clinch another championship this weekend. If he does, Larson will have won back-to-back titles and three championships overall. And somehow, people still argue about whether he gets enough credit. The Numbers Are Getting Hard To Ignore Larson’s 2026 season was not perfect. He endured a lengthy winless stretch before finding his form during the Chase. But that is precisely what makes his current position impressive. He recovered, won multiple postseason races and built a commanding championship lead. Now he heads to Martinsville with a chance to finish the job before the season finale. Where Does Larson Rank Among NASCAR’s Best? This is where the argument gets interesting. Larson’s raw talent has rarely been questioned. His ability to compete across different forms of racing makes him one of the most versatile drivers of his generation. But championships are what separate great seasons from great careers. If Larson clinches Sunday, the conversation about his historical standing becomes harder to avoid. If he falls short, the debate continues. Either way, NASCAR fans should enjoy watching one of the sport’s most gifted drivers build his legacy. The question is no longer whether Larson belongs among the best drivers of his era. It is how high he can climb.

item.title: Alleged plot to shift poll: it’s fake news, we’re unaware — Presidency
item.description: •ADC-PCC insists on allegation plot, warns Tinubu •Reps call for INEC briefing on preparedness By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Luminous Jannamike & Gift ChapiOdekina THE Presidency has described as fake news allegations that the Federal Government was planning to shift the January 16 elections. African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, had earlier raised an alarm over alleged plot to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, into shifting the January 16 presidential election, warning President Bola Tinubu against seeking to evade an electoral verdict. But Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, while reacting to the allegation, said the government was unaware of any move to shift the election. “The federal government is not planning to shift the date of the election or postpone any election. This is not in the works; the federal government is unaware of this, and this is just fake news as far as we are concerned.” However, the council said it had received information that INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, would be summoned to the Presidential Villa and instructed to alter the election timetable, with just 80 days to the poll. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the council urged Tinubu to abandon any such move and called on Amupitan to reject any instruction to change the date and immediately make any such approach public. “The election date belongs to Nigerians. It must not be rewritten behind closed doors at the Villa,” the council said. It said Nigerians had endured three and a half years of soaring prices, shrinking incomes and relentless hardship, insisting that they must be allowed to judge the Tinubu administration at the ballot box on January 16. “A government that has made life this difficult for Nigerians must not be allowed to postpone its day of judgment,” it said. While acknowledging Ebola as a serious public health concern, the council said health professionals must be allowed to contain the disease, adding that INEC must take necessary steps to protect voters and election workers. It cited the position of the Director-General of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, NCDC, that there was currently no reason to postpone the election, warning against using the health emergency as a political justification for delay. The council also put INEC, domestic observers and international election monitors on notice, demanding that any proposal to alter the timetable be made openly, backed by published health evidence and subjected to public scrutiny. “The Presidency must not use a health emergency to escape an electoral verdict,” it added. At press time, the electoral commission was yet to react to the development. Reps to summon INEC for briefing on readiness Meanwhile, the House of Representatives has resolved to invite INEC to appear before its committee to provide a comprehensive assessment of its preparedness for the 2027 general ele

The Rays found the Brewers to be a far tougher opponent than New York or Cleveland, and the Brew Crew have captured their first championship in franchise history. Now, the MLB offseason will commence, and there are several dates to keep an eye on in the months ahead. With the lockout becoming more likely to begin in December, expect to witness a lot of cancellations, alterations, or postponements of important events such as the Winter Meetings, owner meetings, and the draft lottery. If the MLBPA and the owners’ dispute lasts deep into 2027, there’s at least a chance we may not see any baseball at all in the majors in 2027. item.title: Lane Kiffin’s Daughter Is Trending Again, And LSU Fans Have A Lot To Say About It
item.description: Sep 5, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin reacts to a play against Clemson Tigers during the second half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images College football has coaching rumors, playoff debates and rivalry-week arguments. Then there is whatever happens whenever Lane Kiffin’s family enters the social media conversation. Landry Kiffin became a trending topic after appearing to confirm her breakup with LSU linebacker Whit Weeks in a TikTok video. The post showed her brother, Knox, comforting her and jokingly roasting her. It was a personal moment. Naturally, the internet turned it into a college football storyline. The couple had made their relationship public in September 2025. Weeks has not publicly addressed the apparent split. College Football Social Media Has No Offseason Landry was already familiar to college football fans because of her father’s coaching career and her relationship with Weeks. That visibility has only grown as she has developed her own online following and launched her college-inspired clothing brand, Fifth Year. But the breakup discussion shows how quickly personal news can become sports news when a family is connected to a major program. A TikTok that might otherwise remain a personal post suddenly becomes a topic for LSU fans, rival fan bases and people who simply enjoy college football drama. The attention says as much about modern sports culture as it does about the Kiffin family. Can LSU Keep The Conversation On The Field? The Tigers have more pressing concerns than their coach’s daughter’s relationship status. Weeks has been recovering from a serious leg injury, and LSU needs its defense healthy as the season progresses. Kiffin also has to manage the expectations that come with leading one of the sport’s most scrutinized programs. The apparent breakup does not establish anything about team chemistry, coaching decisions or Weeks’ future at LSU. There is no verified evidence that the relationship has affected his role. That distinction matters, even if it makes for a less dramatic rumor. Still, the story is a reminder of the unusual spotlight that follows the Kiffin family. In today’s college football world, the head coach’s press conference is no longer the only place fans look for updates. Sometimes, the next storyline arrives on TikTok.

item.title: Lane Kiffin’s LSU Era Just Got Even More Awkward After His Daughter’s Breakup Post
item.description: Oct 10, 2026; Lexington, Kentucky, USA; LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin walks on the sideline during the first quarter against the Kentucky Wildcats t Kroger Field. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images Lane Kiffin already has enough on his plate trying to build LSU into a championship contender. Now, his daughter’s apparent breakup with one of his own players has become another unexpected storyline surrounding the Tigers. Landry Kiffin appeared to confirm her split from LSU linebacker Whit Weeks in a TikTok posted Oct. 27. The video showed her younger brother, Knox, consoling her after a breakup. Her caption joked about calling on her brother for a humbling experience. The post quickly drew attention from college football fans who had followed her relationship with Weeks. Neither Landry nor Weeks has publicly explained the split in detail. But the post gave fans a new reason to discuss one of LSU’s most unusual off-field connections. Your Head Coach Dating Life Just Became A Football Story Weeks is not just another name on LSU’s roster. He is a senior linebacker and team captain who has earned All-SEC recognition. He also happens to have been dating the head coach’s daughter. That connection was already unusual when Kiffin took over at LSU. Weeks previously explained that the relationship did not affect how Kiffin treated him inside the football program. Now, the apparent breakup has created another layer of attention around a situation that was already guaranteed to attract curiosity. There is no evidence that the relationship has affected Weeks’ standing with the coaching staff. Any suggestion that personal drama will determine his football future would be speculation. Still, the internet was always going to notice this one. LSU Needs Football To Be The Main Story Weeks has been sidelined since suffering a leg fracture against Texas A&M in September. His recovery and eventual return remain much more important to LSU’s defense than his relationship status. Meanwhile, Kiffin has to keep the Tigers focused on the season rather than the latest social media conversation. The situation is awkward enough without anyone turning it into something it is not. Landry is entitled to a private life, and Weeks deserves to be evaluated on his football performance. But when your head coach’s daughter dates one of your team’s biggest defensive stars, even a breakup can become college football news. Welcome to the Lane Kiffin era in Baton Rouge.

item.title: The Atlanta Dream Had A WNBA Championship Within Reach And Watched It Slip Away
item.description: Aug 30, 2026; College Park, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) shoots over Minnesota Lynx forward Natasha Howard (1) during the first half at Gateway Center Arena at College Park. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Dream were two wins away from a championship. Instead, they are left wondering how a promising Finals run unraveled so quickly. Atlanta took a 2-1 lead over the Golden State Valkyries after two convincing victories. Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, while the Dream won Game 3 by 26 points. Then everything changed. Golden State won Game 4, 67-62, before closing the series with a 64-55 victory in Game 5. Atlanta managed only 117 combined points across those final two games. For a team that had championship ambitions, the finish was brutal. The Offense Disappeared When It Mattered Most The Valkyries deserve credit for adjusting defensively. They disrupted Atlanta’s rhythm, contested shots and made the Dream uncomfortable. But Atlanta also struggled to find answers. Reese scored just eight points in Game 4 and seven in Game 5. Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 19 points in Game 4, but the Dream could not generate enough offense to protect their series lead. The shooting numbers told the story. Golden State held Atlanta to 33.3% shooting in Game 4 and followed it with another defensive performance that limited the Dream to 55 points. At that point, blaming one player would miss the bigger problem. Atlanta needed multiple players to step up. It never found the consistent offensive response required to close out the series. This Was An Opportunity The Dream Cannot Take For Granted Reaching the Finals is an accomplishment. Atlanta should not lose sight of that after a painful ending. But the Dream also had a chance to win the franchise’s first championship. They held the lead in the series and had momentum after a dominant Game 3. Golden State adjusted. Atlanta did not respond well enough. That is the lesson the Dream must confront during the offseason. Championship teams need more than a strong start, a dominant star or one impressive win. They need answers when the opponent changes the game. Atlanta came close enough to see the trophy within reach. That makes the final two losses even harder to swallow. The Dream proved they could compete for a championship. Now they must prove this run was the beginning of something bigger, not their best chance gone to waste.

item.title: Angel Reese Went From WNBA Finals Hero To Biggest Question Mark In Two Games
item.description: Aug 30, 2026; College Park, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) reacts after a play against the Minnesota Lynx during the first half at Gateway Center Arena at College Park. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Angel Reese looked like a Finals superstar. Then the Golden State Valkyries found an answer, and Atlanta’s championship hopes took a painful turn. The Atlanta Dream lost 64-55 to Golden State in Game 5 on Monday, ending their title hopes after a series that once looked firmly within reach. Reese had opened the Finals with consecutive dominant performances, including 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2. But the final two games told a different story. Reese scored eight points on 2-of-12 shooting in Game 4, then finished Game 5 with seven points and 15 rebounds. She also committed six turnovers in Game 4 and three in Game 5. Golden State Found The Blueprint The Valkyries made life increasingly difficult for Reese around the basket. Their physical defense disrupted Atlanta’s offensive rhythm and forced the Dream to work for nearly every good look. Reese still contributed on the glass. Her 15 rebounds in Game 5 demonstrated that her impact did not disappear entirely. But rebounding alone could not solve Atlanta’s offensive problems. The Dream scored just 55 points in the decisive game, struggling to generate consistent offense when the stakes were highest. That is the uncomfortable reality of a championship series. Opponents adjust, weaknesses become targets and stars must find ways to respond. The Debate Around Reese Just Got Louder Reese deserves credit for helping Atlanta reach the Finals. Her performances earlier in the series showed why she can be such a difficult matchup. But the final two games will invite uncomfortable questions about her offensive development. Can she remain effective when opponents take away her preferred looks? Can she make defenses pay when the paint becomes crowded? Those are fair basketball questions, not personal attacks. One difficult finish does not define a player’s career. Still, championship opportunities are rare, and Atlanta had a genuine chance to win the title. Reese helped get the Dream there. Now the next step is proving she can help finish the job when defenses have a full series to figure her out.

item.title: Brewers catcher Contreras named World Series MVP
item.description: William Contreras of the Milwaukee Brewers poses with the Willie Mays World Series Most Valuable Player award after the Brewers' title-clinching win over the Tampa Bay Rays (ELSA) Milwaukee's veteran catcher William Contreras was named World Series Most Valuable Player on Wednesday after excelling at the plate and behind it in the Brewers' triumph over the Tampa Bay Rays. Contreras, who became the third Venezuelan to earn World Series MVP honors, hit .382 with four runs-batted-in as the Brewers beat the Rays four games to one in Major League Baseball's best-of-seven championship series. That included a run-scoring double in the sixth inning of the Brewers' 4-1 game-five victory, which clinched the first World Series title in Milwaukee's history. The 28-year-old also caught four Rays stealing, two of them in game one. He confidently shepherded a Brewers pitching staff that stifled the Rays lineup and showed a mastery of the Automated Ball-Strike Challenge System. "I'm very proud. I don't even know what to say," an emotional Contreras said as he received the award. "I have no words to describe what I feel. I just want to thank my teammates. I love this game." The player nicknamed "Wild Bill" established himself as a Major League star 10 years after his elder brother, Willson Contreras, earned a World Series title with the Chicago Cubs. "My brother is my best friend," said Contreras, who shared an embrace with Willson moments after he was named MVP. He joined Pablo Sandoval and Salvador Perez as the third Venezuelan to earn MVP honors. Sandoval did it with the San Francisco Giants in 2012 and Perez with the Kansas City Royals in 2015. He celebrated the championship alongside Brewers teammate Jackson Chourio after the two teamed to help Venezuela win its first World Baseball Classic with a final victory over the United States in March. bb/amz

item.title: Fatigued Devils Fall 5-2 to Avalanche
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 28: Gabriel Landeskog #92 of the Colorado Avalanche scores a second period goal against the New Jersey Devils at Ball Arena on October 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Maclean/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images On a night when even the Devils’ announcers sounded tired, the Devils would have their work cut out for them on the second half of a back-to-back at high altitude. I hope they’ve been doing their cardio. First Period Colorado began the game fast, seemingly to catch the Devils with tired legs on the second half of a back-to-back. For their part, the Devils largely matched the Avalanche’s speed in the first several minutes, showing few signs of fatigue from the night before. Just near the 2:00 mark of the period, Brendan Dillon laid a hit on Nazim Kadri that set the tone for the Devils’ approach for handling the Avalanche tonight – nothing fancy, just get in the way and get it done. On the hit, Kadri was attempting to cross into the Devils’ half of the ice with speed, but Dillon stood him up with a fundamentally solid hit that sent the Devils back in the other direction. At 3:30, a broken play with a bouncing puck turned into a legitimate scoring chance for the Avalanche, but Allen stood tall. He remained sharp a few minutes later, when about halfway through the period, there was a flurry of activity directly in front of him, including a sharp-angle shot from his left that he needed to be ready for. Allen remained strong throughout the period. He looked square to most shots and kept his movement – especially his lateral movement – compact and minimal. Because of this, he managed to be in good position for all of the Avalanche’s shots, making the saves look easy, even on shots coming off the sticks of some of the most talented players in the NHL. Very strong period for Jake, especially since there were one or two scrambles in front of him that never looked particularly dangerous. In one of those scrambles at the 11:00 mark, Brett Pesce took a hooking call on Nathan MacKinnon. I’ll admit that I held my breath when the penalty was assessed. I’ve been impressed with our penalty kill, but this Colorado team is so stacked, their power play (even when in a bit of a slump) is incredibly dangerous. Luckily, Connor Brown had other plans for the Avalanche advantage. While defending in their own zone, Brendan Dillon and Brown were tenacious with their sticks in passing lanes. Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon continually tried to cross the puck from the boards toward the middle of the net, with Dillon and Brown plugging the lanes with their sticks. On one attempt, Brown managed to corral the puck and take a two-on-one the other way with Luke Hughes. As they approached the lower slot area below the dots, Brown attempted to slide a pass from right-to-left to Hughes. The pass deflected off a kneeling Cale Makar and past our old friend Mackenzie Blackwood and into the net for a shorthanded goal. 1-0, Devils

item.title: Paige Spiranac Has Exposed Golf’s Biggest Blind Spot, And The Sport Might Not Like The Answer
item.description: Jul 10, 2019; Los Angeles, CA, USA; Ladies golfer Paige Spiranic arrives on the red carpet at Microsoft Theatre. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Golf has spent decades building its image around tradition, precision and elite competition. Paige Spiranac’s social media success raises an uncomfortable question: Has the sport made itself harder to discover than it needs to be? Spiranac reaches audiences through a style of content that looks nothing like a traditional golf broadcast. Her popularity illustrates how personality-driven coverage can bring the sport into conversations that might otherwise never involve a golf course. That is worth noticing, whether traditional golf media likes it or not. The Problem Is Not Golf. It Is How Golf Gets Presented. The sport has plenty of compelling stories. Rivalries, pressure-packed finishes, equipment debates and the difficulty of playing at the highest level should all make for engaging content. But a casual viewer may not know where to start. A tournament leaderboard can feel distant to someone who does not recognize the players or understand what makes a particular round important. Creators can bridge that gap by making golf feel accessible before asking people to invest hours in a tournament. Spiranac has built a recognizable platform by understanding the internet’s appetite for personality-driven content. Traditional Golf Media Should Not Ignore The Lesson This is not an argument that social media personalities are more important than professional golfers. The athletes remain the center of the competition. It is an argument that attracting attention is its own skill. Golf can protect its traditions while finding better ways to reach casual fans. Short videos, accessible explanations and recognizable personalities can help introduce new audiences to the game. Spiranac’s success offers a reminder that people do not always discover sports through the sports themselves. Sometimes they discover them through the people who make them interesting. Golf should treat that as an opportunity, not a threat.

item.title: FG approves East, West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW
item.description: •Pays N1.23trn of N3.3trn power sector debt By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA—THE Federal Government said yesterday it has approved the commencement of procurement for the proposed East and West super grids, as part of efforts to strengthen the national electricity network and raise transmission capacity from about 5,000 megawatts to 19,000MW within two years. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents at the end of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu, at the Council Chamber, Presidential Villa, Abuja. He explained that the projects would improve grid resilience and enable the country evacuate more electricity to consumers. “The East and West Super Grids are not projects for one part of the country. They cut across the north and south of Nigeria, strengthening the backbone that must carry power from where it is generated to where it is needed,’’ he said. The initiative is designed to address one of the sector’s central contradictions: Nigeria has more than 13,000MW of available generation capacity, but its transmission network can reliably wheel only about 5,000MW. Tegbe said the super grids would improve resilience, reduce grid instability and allow more electricity to reach homes, businesses and industries. He said: “The target is simple. We want a grid that can evacuate the power we already have, not one that leaves generation stranded while consumers remain in darkness.’’ The minister explained that the corridors would strengthen transmission links from Sokoto through Abuja and other locations into parts of southern Nigeria. Beyond the super grids, the council approved three immediate interventions for Abuja and the Lagos axis, two of the country’s most important electricity demand centres. The first is a 33kV double-circuit underground and overhead line connected to the Katampe Transmission Substation, a major hub serving the North-Central region. The second covers the design, manufacture and supply of three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation, a critical node supplying Lagos. The third will reconstruct and upgrade the 35.6-kilometre Itumola–Mapasin–Shagamu 132kV single-circuit line into a double-circuit line to serve rising demand along the Lagos–Shagamu corridor. “These are not glamorous projects, but they are the projects that determine whether power actually gets to the consumer,” Tegbe said. On sector liquidity, the minister disclosed that the federal government had paid N1.23 trillion of the N3.3 trillion owed gas suppliers and other power-sector stakeholders. “We have paid N1.23 trillion, and we intend to finish the job. But we must also stop new debts from accumulating,’’ he said. The post FG approves East, West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NFL Trade Deadline 2026: Top 10 Candidates and Potential Destinations Ft. Saquon Barkley to Minnesota Vikings
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley. © IMAGN The NFL Trade Deadline is around the corner on Nov. 10 at 4:00 pm EST, which leaves less time than one would think for teams to put their affairs in order. Some moves have already happened, like Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the Houston Texans. However, there are plenty more moves ahead with about two weeks left until the trade deadline. Here’s a look at the top 10 candidates likely to be traded at the deadline, including Maxx Crosby, Saquon Barkley and Stefon Diggs. The list is in order of the chances of it happening. Every player on this list is at risk, but some are more at risk than others. Top 10 NFL Trade Deadline Candidates by Likelihood #10 – Maxx Crosby, DE, Las Vegas Raiders If not for a bizarrely failed physical, Maxx Crosby would be wearing a Baltimore Ravens jersey. However, halfway through the season, his future isn’t set in stone. If the Raiders lose their next two matchups after already losing four straight, the Raiders could be sellers at the deadline. Moving Crosby could help the team get the capital needed to build around Fernando Mendoza in the offseason. Potential destinations: Jaguars, Packers, Cowboys, Bills #9 – Saquon Barkley, RB, Philadelphia Eagles Saquon Barkley is trapped in purgatory on a team going nowhere fast with Jalen Hurts shut down for the season due to his blood clot issue (ESPN). Barkley, set to turn 30 in about the next 100 days on Feb. 9, may not want to burn a year waiting to see if the Eagles can rebound next season or if Hurts will ever be the same. It could be years before Philadelphia’s next Super Bowl window. This might push Barkley to quietly ask for an exit behind closed doors so he can chase one more ring before he reaches the undisputed end of his prime. Potential destinations: Jaguars, Vikings #8 – Calvin Ridley, WR, Tennessee Titans Calvin Ridley has been stuck in a strange place as a depth receiver on the Tennessee Titans. It seems like both he and the team are going nowhere, and the Titans will have every reason to do what they can to generate some additional draft capital. Ridley might still be worth something, which could push the Titans to move the receiver. Potential destinations: Broncos, Bills, 49ers #7 – Ladd McConkey, WR, Los Angeles Chargers Ladd McConkey’s Chargers are the last winless team in the NFL, which means that seemingly everything is on the table. If the Chargers are going to rebuild this offseason, moving McConkey could be one way to help speed up the reloading process. item.title: Paige Spiranac Could Post About Golf And Still Outdraw Half The Sport’s Biggest Names
item.description: Jul 10, 2019; Los Angeles, CA, USA; Ladies golfer Paige Spiranic arrives on the red carpet at Microsoft Theatre. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Golf has a visibility problem that Paige Spiranac seems uniquely equipped to solve. Major tournaments can produce incredible drama, elite athletic performances and historic moments. Yet plenty of casual fans still scroll past golf content without giving it a second look. Spiranac has found a way to reach those audiences by combining golf knowledge, personality and an unmistakable social media presence. Golf’s Online Game Looks Different Traditional golf coverage often revolves around scores, course strategy and tournament results. Spiranac’s content reaches people who might not regularly watch four days of competitive golf. That audience matters. Sports are competing for attention against everything else on the internet. A personality who gets people interested in golf outside tournament weekends can help introduce the game to new fans. Spiranac’s success also highlights a reality that traditional sports media sometimes overlooks: accessibility and personality can be just as important as technical analysis when attracting casual viewers. The Sport Should Pay Attention Golf does not need to abandon its traditions to embrace a wider audience. It can respect the competition while experimenting with different ways to tell its stories. Spiranac demonstrates how an individual creator can make golf more approachable online. That does not mean every player needs to become an influencer or every broadcast needs to change its formula. It does mean the sport should recognize what captures attention beyond the fairway. The next generation of golf fans may not discover the game through a major championship. They might discover it through a creator who makes them curious enough to watch one.

item.title: Former NFL Coach Lovie Smith Caught In Heated Confrontation With High School Parents
item.description: USA TODAY Sports Former NFL head coach Lovie Smith was caught on video in a heated confrontation with parents of players at an Arizona high school earlier this month, adding another chapter to a growing controversy surrounding the football program. Smith, whose son Miles is the head coach at Desert Ridge High School in Mesa, Arizona, recently joined the coaching staff. Video shared by The Main Event Show appears to show the former NFL coach confronting parents after football equipment was thrown onto the locker room floor and a photo of the scene was taken. item.title: Alexander Volkanovski Willing to Vacate Featherweight Title to Fight Arman Tsarukyan for Lightweight Gold if Justin Gaethje Retires
item.description: It looks like Alexander Volkanovski wants that second UFC belt no matter what. The Aussie recently floated the idea of a retirement fight against Justin Gaethje for the lightweight title. However, with Gaethje’s UFC future still up in the air, Volk has also expressed interest in running it back with Ilia Topuria at 155lbs . Now, with Arman Tsarukyan back in the lightweight title picture, Volkanovski has another name in mind. The featherweight champion is willing to fight the Armenian if Gaethje decides to retire and vacate the lightweight belt. The idea has become more realistic after Volk’s UFC 333 title defense against Movsar Evloev and Dana White’s positive response to his lightweight ambitions. Alexander Volkanovski Growing More Excited About Potential Arman Tsarukyan Title Fight Speaking to Ariel Helwani recently, Volk acknowledged Tsarukyan’s position in the title race and made it clear he would have no problem sharing the Octagon with the Armenian. “I do believe Arman should be fighting for the title. If I was in the lightweight division and I was champion at lightweight, I’m fighting Arman 100%.” He added, “And if Gaethje don’t want to do that, I’ll do it. Again you got Ilia and Paddy in a great position, but I think that’s [Ilia vs. Paddy] a great fight. That excites me; it’s because Arman’s a great fighter. Everyone knows how I do against wrestlers. Everyone knows I can handle wrestlers. I think he’s one of the best wrestlers and grapplers in the UFC, but you ain’t holding me down. Even Arman.” Volk also explained why a matchup with Tsarukyan appeals to him. While he respects the Armenian’s wrestling and grappling, the Aussie believes he can handle the challenge and make it an exciting fight. Volk: “If I was champion at lightweight, I’m fighting Arman. 100%. If Gaethje doesn’t wanna do that, I’ll do it. Me versus Arman for the belt. That excites me. Everyone knows how I do against wrestlers. Everyone knows I can handle wrestlers. I think he’s one of the best wrestlers and grapplers in the UFC, but you ain’t holding me down. I’ve got so much respect for him, but I’m getting back up, and we’re standing and fighting. He’s got good stand-up too, so that’ll be a fun fight. item.title: Angel Reese Is One Of Basketball’s Biggest Stars, So Why Does Every Conversation About Her Turn Into A Fight?
item.description: Sep 30, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) dribbles the ball against the Washington Mystics during the third quarter of game two of the first round for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs at CareFirst Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rafael Suanes-Imagn Images There are plenty of basketball players worth discussing. Somehow, Angel Reese can turn an ordinary sports conversation into a full-blown argument. Her supporters see a confident star with the potential to keep growing. Her critics question her game, her public persona or the amount of attention she receives. Then social media takes over, and the original basketball discussion often disappears. The Internet Cannot Agree On Angel Reese Reese occupies a unique place in women’s basketball because she attracts strong reactions from both sides. Her fans defend her aggressively, while her detractors rarely miss an opportunity to criticize her. That dynamic can make even routine basketball news feel like a referendum on her entire career. It also creates an obvious problem for anyone trying to evaluate her fairly. The loudest opinions are not always the most informed ones. A player’s performance can be good, bad or somewhere in between without proving every argument made about her. Being Polarizing Is Part Of The Business Now Modern sports stars compete for attention as much as they compete on the court. Reese has become particularly effective at drawing that attention. The challenge is making sure the conversation remains connected to basketball. Her production, development and role in the WNBA deserve serious analysis. So does the way her popularity brings new eyes to the league. Fans can disagree about how good Reese is right now. But the constant arguing around her reveals something larger about sports culture: sometimes, the debate becomes the product. And Reese remains one of the clearest examples.

item.title: ‘He’s Always Paranoid,’ ‘You’re Walking on Eggshells’ — Pat McAfee’s Former Employee Exposes What ESPN Star Is Really Like Behind the Scenes
item.description: ‘He's Always Paranoid,’ ‘You’re Walking On Eggshells’ — Pat McAfee’s Former Employee Exposes What ESPN Star Is Really Like Behind the Scenes Pat McAfee’s bold personality and outspoken nature have made him one of the most recognizable (and polarizing) figures in sports media. But according to McAfee’s former colleague Jeff “Vibbs” Vibbert, working for the ESPN star was “exhausting.” Vibbert worked with McAfee at Barstool Heartland (the company’s Indianapolis office) for a little over a year from 2017 to 2018, and he recently shared his experience working for the former NFL punter. Jeff Vibbert Details What It Was Like Working With Pat McAfee The comments come after McAfee sparked controversy over his reaction to a video posted by the University of Utah’s official Instagram account. The clip featured students describing McAfee as “corny” and doing impressions of the ESPN star. McAfee said on “College GameDay” that he hoped to “never return” to the college. He later blasted the school on his show, saying he felt “uncomfortable” and unsafe on campus, which led to backlash online. The university eventually deleted the video and issued an apology. But Vibbs said McAfee’s reaction didn’t surprise him, pointing to a pattern of paranoia and unpredictable moods he experienced while working with him. “I think that paranoia is who he is,” Vibbs said on the “Out & About” podcast. “Like, he’s always paranoid. When we were working there, you’re just kind of walking on eggshells, wondering what he’s going to be like emotionally when he shows up. Who’s he going to be mad at? Who’s he going to be feuding with? “You have to co-sign the paranoia and be [like], ‘Yep, you’re very valid in what you’re thinking…’ You were just, like, never allowed to go at him or say anything… ’cause if he felt a slight, he’d react,” he added. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Reflecting on his time at the Indianapolis-based Barstool office, Vibbs described a workplace where staff had to be mindful of McAfee’s reactions. While there were enjoyable moments, he suggested that tensions and indirect communication made the experience difficult. “Pat would just be like, ‘Oh, yeah, we’re fine,’ and then talk [expletive] behind your back,” Vibbs said. “And it was like, ‘All right, dude. Like, just say what’s going on.’ It was exhausting. It was not a good time.” When asked whether he missed working with McAfee, Vibbs made it clear that he doesn’t and initially said “there’s no amount of money” that could convince him to go back. Vibbs eventually conceded with a laugh, “Okay, alright. item.title: Angel Reese Critics Keep Moving The Goalposts, And WNBA Fans Have Had Enough
item.description: Sep 27, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) reacts after a foul call against the Washington Mystics in the fourth quarter during game one of the first round for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs at State Farm Arena. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Angel Reese seems to face a new set of expectations every time she steps on a basketball court. For some critics, the standard never stops changing. When Reese rebounds, the conversation can shift to scoring. When she scores, the discussion can turn to efficiency. When she speaks confidently, the debate can become about personality instead of basketball. At some point, fans have to ask whether they are evaluating a player or simply reacting to a celebrity. Criticism Is Fair. Changing The Standard Is Not. Reese is not above criticism. No professional athlete is, and her performances should be judged honestly. But meaningful analysis requires consistent standards. A player should not be praised for one skill one day and dismissed for that same skill the next. Reese’s rebounding, offensive development and overall impact are all legitimate subjects for discussion. So is how her game compares with other top players in the league. The conversation gets weaker when every performance becomes an excuse to recycle the same argument. The Debate Says Something About The WNBA Reese’s popularity means her performances attract viewers who might not otherwise follow the league closely. That attention creates opportunities, even when the conversation becomes unnecessarily personal. The WNBA needs stars who generate interest. It also needs coverage that can distinguish a rough game from a larger career judgment. Fans do not have to agree about Reese. They should at least be able to agree on what they are evaluating. If every game becomes another referendum on her entire existence as a basketball player, the analysis has probably gone too far.

item.title: How Bengals compare to Chiefs, Steelers in honoring legends | Williams
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals have made their team hall of fame more exclusive. Any hall of fame should be exclusive and set a high bar to gain membership, and the Bengals are falling more in line with how some of the elite organizations in the AFC induct former players and major team contributors into their version of Cincinnati’s Ring of Honor. But some Bengals fans and former players remain upset about the club’s decision to drop to one ROH inductee per year beginning in 2027. They want to know why, especially since the Bengals didn’t launch their Ring of Honor until 2021 after years of fans pleading for them to join the modern NFL and follow most franchises in officially recognizing past players and other significant club contributors. ROH member Willie Anderson took to social media in July and implored the Bengals to continue to induct multiple members each year. Fans and former players believe the Bengals need to continue to play catch-up by inducting multiple people each year. The Bengals, however, aren’t directly answering questions about their decision ahead of James Brooks and the late Bob Trumpy going into the Ring of Honor at halftime of the Nov. 1 game against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium. The Bengals declined to make executive Elizabeth Blackburn available to answer questions when I reached out. Blackburn oversees the ROH. Instead, I was sent links to press releases on the Bengals’ official website from May, when the announcement was made that changes were coming for the ROH. The Bengals have a right to do as they please with their ROH. They’ve come a long way in being more fan-friendly and officially acknowledging their history after decades of publicly showing they didn’t seem to care. They let season ticket holders vote on the ROH nominees each season, a great decision that will continue, a club official said. It'd still be good to offer fans a full explanation about why the change was made and why now. Nonetheless, here is what Blackburn said about the change, per Bengals.com: "The Ring of Honor is a special tradition for fans, Season Ticket Members and Bengals alumni. To add to the Ring of Honor's prestige and significance, we felt this evolution after its fifth season was appropriate, thoughtful and a positive move." Blackburn also pointed out that most teams induct one member a year into their version of the ROH. Generally, I like the move. The Bengals don’t have a rich enough tradition of excellence to continue to induct multiple people in the Ring of Honor each season. Even some of the AFC’s most storied franchises either induct only one person each season or skip years without enshrining anyone in their team hall of fame. The Bengals, who’ve never won a Super Bowl, have three members in their ROH who are also in the Pro Football Hall of Fame – Anthony Munoz, Ken Riley and Paul Brown. item.title: Angel Reese Somehow Turns Every WNBA Debate Into A Bigger Story Than The Game Itself
item.description: Oct 17, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) between plays against the Golden State Valkyries during the fourth quarter of game one of the 2026 WNBA Finals at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Angel Reese does not need to score 30 points to become the center of a basketball conversation. Sometimes, the conversation around her becomes almost as big as the game itself. That is part of what makes Reese such a fascinating figure in the WNBA. Her game, confidence, public comments and social media presence consistently draw attention from fans who rarely agree on anything about her. Basketball Has Become A 24-Hour Debate Reese is one of the league’s most recognizable personalities, and that visibility comes with a strange trade-off. Every accomplishment can trigger praise, while every mistake can become a national argument. Some fans view her as a star helping grow women’s basketball. Others question whether the attention matches her production. Both sides keep the conversation alive. The result is a player whose impact on the sports conversation extends well beyond the box score. That does not mean every debate is fair or particularly insightful. It does mean Reese has become impossible to ignore. The Attention Is Not Going Away Women’s basketball has benefited from personalities who can bring casual fans into the sport. Reese is clearly one of them. The challenge is separating meaningful basketball analysis from the endless cycle of online arguments. Fans can debate her performance, her ceiling and her place among the league’s biggest stars. But pretending she is not a major draw makes little sense. Love her or criticize her, Angel Reese has mastered one part of modern sports: getting people to pay attention.

For new coach Jerrod Calhoun, who guided Utah State to back-to-back NCAA Tournament appearances, the ultimate goal is to return his alma mater to "The Dance." Since their last invitation in 2019 under Mick Cronin, the Bearcats have been bystanders. Now with a flipped roster outside of walk-on Grant Darbyshire, Calhoun hopes his "We over Me" message, depth and ball movement will return UC to March Madness. Game-by-game predictions for Cincinnati Bearcats basketball in 2026-27 In full disclosure, The Enquirer has overestimated UC the past two seasons. They were ranked preseason No. 20 in 2024-25 but tanked in the Big 12 in January. Our 24-7 regular-season guess finished at 19-16 with an appearance in The Crown tournament in Las Vegas. National prognosticators backed off in 2025-26, though UC had personnel changes and a deceiving preseason win over eventual national champion Michigan in Ann Arbor. We predicted 23-8, which turned into 18-15 and the end of the road for Wes Miller. Ten days later, Calhoun was hired. He has flipped a roster. From Utah State, Elijah Perryman, Adlan Elamin, David Iweze and MJ Collins have NCAA experience from last year. Ditto Eric Mahaffey and Amani Lyles from Akron. Darbyshire went dancing at Kentucky, Myles Colvin played in a national title game at Purdue before leaving for Wake Forest, and Riley Allenspach played in the NCAA Tournament for Samford before going to George Mason. item.title: Deputy Senate President faults Osinbajo over alleged comments on gloomy economy, democracy
item.description: *Says Tinubu addressing long-standing challenges By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, APC, Kano North, has taken a swipe at former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo over the gloomy picture he painted of Nigeria’s economy and democratic governance. Senator Barau Jibrin who noted that Osinbajo got it wrong , said the administration of President Bola Tinubu was taking steps to address what he described as longstanding challenges confronting the country. According to Jibrin, while Osinbajo’s concerns, particularly those drawn from Afrobarometer surveys on Nigeria and other African countries were valid, the government needed to improve communication with the people to highlight ongoing efforts to address the challenges. Recall that Osinbajo, who served as Vice-President under former President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2023, had expressed concern in his lecture about the failure of democratic governance among citizens across Africa after almost three decades of uninterrupted democratic rule in several countries. Citing Afrobarometer surveys, Osinbajo, who was defeated by President Bola Tinubu during APC presidential primary, ahead of the 2023 elections, highlighted widespread dissatisfaction with democratic institutions, economic hardship, declining public confidence in government and diminishing youth participation in electoral politics. He noted that although 64 per cent of Africans preferred democracy to other forms of government, only 38 per cent were satisfied with the way democracy was working in their respective countries. Osinbajo also cited findings indicating that 59 per cent of Africans considered their national economies to be in bad shape, while 51 per cent said their economies had deteriorated. He further expressed concern over the rising cost of living, unemployment, inadequate access to healthcare and declining voter turnout, warning that persistent hardship could weaken public confidence in democracy, particularly among young people. But replying the former vice president at a public lecture, titled ‘’Democracy and Development: Rethinking the Leadership Question,’’ in Yola, Adamawa State, to commemorate the 59th birthday of Governor Ahmadu Fintiri yesterday, Barau described Osinbajo’s lecture as thought-provoking and intellectually stimulating. He,however, said the gloomy picture painted by the surveys was being addressed and that the gaps were partly attributable to inadequate communication between governments and citizens. He said: “I know he is a very good orator, a good public speaker and an intellectual to the core. Having said that, I am compelled to make some comments on the paper. It is a very beautiful and thought-provoking paper. “What I want to say is this: one important reason for the gloomy picture portrayed by the surveys, particularly those conducted by Afrobarometer, is what the professor talked about and specifically observed: the issue of communication between the leaders and the

item.title: Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski diagnosed with right calf sprain after sixth inning exit vs. Brewers
item.description: Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski diagnosed with right calf sprain after sixth inning exit vs. Brewers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jacob Misiorowski has well and truly given it his all for the Milwaukee Brewers , leading them to the franchise’s first World Series title. Despite all the clamor for him to appear late in Game 4, it looks as though the Brewers made the right call to save him for Game 5 — with Misiorowski giving the Brewers 5.2 innings of shutout baseball to put Milwaukee in position to win against the Tampa Bay Rays. After exiting the contest, a report from Bob Nightengale of USA Today mentioned that Misiorowski had suffered a right calf sprain , which would put his status for the rest of the World Series, should it go beyond Game 5, in doubt. Misiorowski did not appear to have his best stuff on Wednesday, as he struck out only two batters during his time on the mound. Nonetheless, he got the Brewers 17 crucial outs, giving their overtaxed bullpen some time to rest after Milwaukee burned through their relievers in their 12-inning loss in Game 4. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Brewers’ bullpen, of course, ended up protecting the lead. JoJo Romero and Abner Uribe combined to pitch 1.1 innings of shutout baseball, bridging the gap from Misiorowski to closer Trevor Megill, who would end up getting the final six outs of the game. Misiorowski has been brilliant for the Brewers all season long, and Milwaukee is now a World Series champion after grabbing the victory in a game where their ace got the win. In four postseason starts in 2026, Misiorowski allowed just four earned runs in 19.0 innings of work, good for an ERA of 1.89. The Brewers won all four of his starts, and this explains why manager Pat Murphy was so adamant in his decision to preserve him for Game 5. Misiorowski better rest up his calf in preparation for all the jumping he’s about to do in celebration of the franchise’s first World Series title. item.title: Steph Curry ties LeBron James with epic piece of history
item.description: Stephen Curry tied LeBron James in a 40-plus point shooting performance Wednesday night. Steph Curry continues to put himself in the greatness category. During the Warriors’ 119-114 victory against the host Timberwolves on Wednesday night, Curry put himself into the same scoring category as LeBron James. Curry tied James at 15 games for 40-point game performances past the age of 35 years old. Stephen Curry tied LeBron James for 40+ point games past the age of 35 following 44 point performance against the Timberwolves. AP Photo/Abbie Parr Stephen Curry ties LeBron James for games with 40+ points past the age 35. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect From the moment the game tipped off, Curry was on fire. The 38-year-old had 23 points through the first half, and it continued into the second half, as Golden State had a 24-point lead, when he checked out at the 5:01 mark of the third quarter. Curry also finished 16 of 16 at the free-throw line. Besides scoring a lot, Curry also had eight rebounds and six assists. Rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg had his highest-scoring performance, finishing with 26 points, sinking 2 of 5 3-pointers and shooting 55% from the field. Golden State went up against a Timberwolves team that was without Anthony Edwards, who will miss at least the next two months due to arthroscopic surgery on his right knee . Stephen Curry lined up at the free-throw line in a 44-point performance where he shot 16 of 16 from the free-throw line. NBAE via Getty Images Luca Evans of The San Francisco Chronicle reported that Steve Kerr said the Warriors “smelled blood in the water.” After starting the season 0-3, Golden State is starting to find its rhythm and has won two in a row. The Warriors will take the court again on Friday, when they host the Lakers.

item.title: Cooper Flagg, Dallas Mavericks send short-handed OKC Thunder to first loss of NBA season
item.description: DALLAS — Wednesday was supposed to be a proper homecoming for Cason Wallace . It was supposed to be his first game back in Dallas, the area he grew up in, as a full-time starter for OKC . And he was supposed to get some love when his name was announced by the American Airlines Center crowd. But when the Thunder's starters were named prior to a road game against the Dallas Mavericks , Wallace wasn't suited up. He instead wore a grey sweatsuit with a sling on his left arm, supporting a torn labrum in his left shoulder that he sustained against the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday. The rest of OKC's team didn't receive a warm welcome to Dallas either. Its short trip across state lines was a reminder of how quickly things can go south during the NBA season. The Thunder suffered a 120-96 loss to the Mavericks on a night when it was without Chet Holmgren (right knee patellar tendinitis), Jalen Williams (left ankle fracture), Wallace (left shoulder labral tear), Alex Caruso (right ankle sprain), Nikola Topić (low back surgery) and Thomas Sorber (right knee surgery). Ajay Mitchell led OKC with 29 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals on 12-for-20 shooting from the field (2 for 5 from deep) in 27 minutes. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander also added 21 points, six rebounds and two assists on 7-for-19 shooting from the field (1 for 6 from deep) in 28 minutes. Next up for OKC (4-1) is a road game against the Houston Rockets (5-0) at 7:30 p.m. CT Saturday (NBA TV). Here are three takeaways from the loss: Thunder vs Mavericks live updates: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, OKC visit Cooper Flagg, Dallas Aday Mara faced off against former Michigan family Dusty May has always been in Aday Mara's corner. He believed in him back in April 2025, when May was Michigan's head coach and Mara had just transferred to the program. And he believed in him leading up to the 2026 NBA Draft, where OKC selected the big man with the No. 12 pick . May still believes in Mara to this day, too. But now that he's the head coach at Dallas, he just had to put that support on pause Wednesday. "After tonight, I hope he continues to play incredibly well," May said with a smile before the game. Unfortunately, Mara didn't extend that courtesy to his former coach. The lengthy center instead made an impact right when he checked in midway through the first quarter, as he blocked a layup by former Michigan teammate Morez Johnson Jr. Mara continued to contribute during his limited minutes. He showed flashes of his rim protecting and finishing skills by recording six points, three rebounds and two blocks on 2-for-4 shooting from the field in 20 minutes. Mara could see an uptick in moments moving forward. Especially if OKC continues to be without Holmgren, who missed a second straight game Wednesday due to right knee patellar tendinitis.
