item.title: Bears’ Caleb Williams will still wear Caddix cleats to prevent injuries despite NFL fine
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Bears’ Caleb Williams will still wear Caddix cleats to prevent injuries despite NFL fine appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coming into the 2026 season, the Chicago Bears would have been hoping that star quarterback Caleb Williams would take another leap. Williams improved a ton in 2025 in his first season working with Ben Johnson, and he has continued that growth so far in 2026. Now, he looks like one of the future stars of the NFL. Unfortunately for Williams, his 2026 season was interrupted in Week 2 when he suffered a hamstring injury that caused him to miss three games. Since he has been back, he has been wearing Caddix cleats, which are designed to be easier on your legs and prevent injuries. Despite the good intentions, the NFL fined him nearly $12,000 for wearing unapproved cleats. Williams doesn’t care about the fine. On Wednesday, he revealed that he is willing to take the fine and will continue to wear Caddix cleats to maximize his ability to stay on the field, via Ari Meirov. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “They are a science-type of cleat. It’s something that focuses on when you plant on the hard plants on turf or grass, they call them SmartStuds, and they move when you move,” Williams said. “They take tension off of your tendons, your joints and all of that. … “I’m focused on being able to be out here for the guys. And if that can give me a small percentage up and it works, then that’s what I’m gonna do.” Williams is essential to the Bears’ hopes of chasing a Super Bowl this season and over the next decade, so it comes as no surprise to see both him and the team prioritizing his health. Caddix, despite not sponsoring Williams, has said that it will pay his fine, at least for the first week. The former No. 1 overall pick is having the best season of his career so far in 2026 and has the Bears off to a 5-2 start . In four games, he has completed 71% of his passes for 1,020 yards and five touchdowns with just one interception. He also has two rushing touchdowns. Williams will have another chance to show off his skills on Monday Night Football in Week 8 against the Seattle Seahawks. item.title: Manufacturers raise alarm over N1.35trn alternative power costs, 18,935 job losses
item.description: *Say growth crawls at 1.41%, despite broader economic recovery *Urge FG to cut energy, financing costs lAcknowledge govt’s import-duty, value-added tax relief on 875 pharmaceutical raw materials By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Omotola Aremo LAGOS — Manufacturers under the aegis of Chemical and Non-Metallic Products Employers Federation, CANMPEF, said yesterday they were facing mounting pressure from soaring energy costs, expensive credit, weak consumer demand and job losses, despite improvements in the country’s key macro-economic indicators in 2025. The federation also raised alarm over the worsening cost of doing business, citing an estimated N1.35 trillion spent by local manufacturers on alternative power in 2025, alongside the loss of 18,935 manufacturing jobs in the first half of the year. President of CANMPEF and Vice President of the Dangote Group, Chief Devakumar Edwin, who raised the alarm at the Federation’s 46th Annual General Meeting, AGM, in Lagos, called on the Federal Government to urgently address the high cost of energy and financing, harmonise taxes and levies and strengthen support for local production. He said: “Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.87 per cent in 2025, up from 3.38 per cent in 2024, while headline inflation declined and the foreign exchange market became more stable. However, these improvements have yet to translate into meaningful gains for manufacturers. “Manufacturing grew by only 1.41 per cent in 2025, compared with 1.20 per cent in 2024, while its contribution to real Gross Domestic Product fell to 8.05 per cent from 8.24 per cent.’’ Edwin described the situation as a major concern for the industrial sector, stressing that macro-economic stability must translate into stronger industrial output, job creation and export growth. “Our central message is that this stability must now translate into competitiveness in the form of sustainable jobs, increased output and exports. ‘’Although the economic reforms introduced from mid-2023 had delivered measurable improvements in inflation, foreign exchange stability and economic growth, manufacturers continue to grapple with high operating costs that undermined production and investment. Most of these gains have yet to reach the factory floor,” the CANMPEF president stated. ‘Electricity supply is major constraint’ He identified electricity supply as one of the most significant constraints confronting manufacturers, particularly producers of chemicals, plastics, rubber, glass, ceramics and other non-metallic mineral products, many of which depended on energy-intensive production processes. “Despite installed grid capacity exceeding 13,000 megawatts, average delivered generation remained below 5,000MW, against estimated demand of about 18,345MW. The shortfall, attributed to gas-supply constraints, transmission bottlenecks and recurring grid collapses, has forced many manufacturers to depend on alternative power sources at considerable expense,’’ Edwin said. item.title: 44 YEARS OF HEARTBREAK ARE OVER! THE MILWAUKEE BREWERS JUST DELIVERED ONE OF THE GREATEST POSTSEASONS IN BASEBALL HISTORY
item.description: Oct 28, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio (11) holds the World Series trophy after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images For 44 years, Milwaukee has waited for another chance to celebrate a World Series championship. Generations of Brewers fans have grown up hearing about the 1982 team, wondering what it would feel like to watch their own team reach the very top of baseball. Now, they finally have their answer. The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to complete one of the most memorable postseason runs the sport has ever seen. But this championship is about so much more than the final score. It’s about the city, the fans who never gave up, the veterans who spent years chasing this moment, the young stars who rose to the occasion, and a team that seemed to find a hero every time it needed one. This is the story of how Milwaukee finally got its moment. 44 YEARS LATER, MILWAUKEE FINALLY HAS ITS CHAMPIONSHIP The last time the Brewers played in the World Series was 1982. That team came heartbreakingly close to winning it all before falling to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games. For decades, that series remained a part of the franchise’s identity. The memories of Robin Yount, Paul Molitor and that unforgettable team became something older fans passed down to younger generations. There were plenty of talented Brewers teams in the years that followed. There were playoff appearances, division titles and seasons that gave fans genuine hope. But the ultimate prize remained out of reach. Until now. The 2026 Brewers didn’t just end that wait. They did it with a 103-win regular season and an 11-2 postseason record, defeating the Padres, sweeping the Dodgers and finishing the job against the Rays. After so many years of coming up short, Milwaukee finally has a championship team of its own. And somewhere, the fans who spent their lives waiting for this moment are finally able to say they witnessed it. THIS CHAMPIONSHIP BELONGS TO THE CITY OF MILWAUKEE Perhaps the most emotional part of this entire run was watching the city rally behind its team. When the Brewers traveled to Tampa Bay for Games 3 through 5, Milwaukee didn’t simply turn on the television and hope for the best. Fans packed American Family Field for watch parties, selling out all three events. Approximately 31,000 people attended each of the watch parties for Games 3, 4 and 5. They filled the ballpark to watch their team compete for a championship, even though the actual games were being played more than 1,000 miles away. Think about that for a moment. More than 30,000 people repeatedly showed up to watch a game on a screen because they wanted to feel connected to something bigger than themselves. item.title: JJ Redick reveals Jarred Vanderbilt plan amid Luka Doncic, Ziaire Williams injuries
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images JJ Redick reveals Jarred Vanderbilt plan amid Luka Doncic, Ziaire Williams injuries appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers were hit with a double whammy prior to their game against the LA Clippers on Wednesday evening when it was announced that both Luka Doncic and Ziaire Williams were ruled out due to injury concerns. With the Lakers needing roster depth, especially in the front-court, head coach JJ Redick acknowledged that he was considering turning to a familiar face in Jarred Vanderbilt. Ahead of the Lakers’ game against the Clippers, JJ Redick admitted that it was not ideal to play Jarred Vanderbilt at backup center, but that situation might call for it. The Lakers are in the midst of a grueling stretch of five games in seven nights and have been pushed to the limit in terms of consistent center depth. “I think my conversations with Vando last year were a lot about putting him in a position to succeed … the second half of the Luka’s first season with us post-trade, just for position, we didn’t have anybody outside of Jaxson [Hayes] who could really play. So he did that by necessity,” Redick said during his pregame press conference. “I think he’s better suited obviously to be more of a wing and a forward and be out on the perimeter defensively. But there’s going to be moments where he’s going to, by necessity, have to play some five.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Coming into the game against the Clippers, Vanderbilt had yet to play in any of the Lakers’ first four games. Behind Austin Reaves, he’s the second-longest tenured player on the team. Back during training camp, Redick pointed to an example of Vanderbilt having a strong practice day due to his familiarity with the system and what the coaching staff wants on the court. But it’s been hard at times for the nine-year veteran to crack the rotation over the past couple of seasons. He’s tended to play a regular role during the season, but his playing time has decreased in each of the past two playoffs. He’s coming off a season in which he appeared in 65 games, including three starts, at a little over 17 minutes per game. He averaged 4.4 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists with splits of 47.1 percent shooting from the field, 29.3 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 58.9 percent shooting from the free-throw line. With the Lakers in need of depth to provide defense and rebounding , two of Vanderbilt’s strengths, he has a prime opportunity that even with Doncic and Williams’ injuries not expected to be concerning, to prove he should stick in the rotation. item.title: Arnab Strikes India
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Arnab Strikes India Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search The first named storm of the 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season—Arnab (pronounced Or-nab)—emerged in the Bay of Bengal on October 25, a rather late start for a basin that typically produces named cyclones in April or May. When the VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) on NOAA-20 captured this nighttime image at 20:12 Universal Time on October 26 (1:42 a.m. India Standard Time on October 27), the storm had sustained winds of about 140 kilometers (85 miles) per hour, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). When Arnab made landfall on the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast early on October 28, sustained winds were 130 kilometers per hour. IMD categorizes a storm that strength as a “very severe cyclonic storm ,” which is similar to a Category 1 storm on the Saffir-Simpson hurricane wind scale . It made landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, a heavily settled area home to large cities, farmland, and fishing communities. Arnab caused extensive damage, uprooting trees, inundating crops and homes, limiting fishing operations, and disrupting transportation and power networks, according to news reports . Prior to landfall, Indian authorities had evacuated tens of thousands of people from vulnerable coastal areas. The storm comes in the midst of an El Niño , a climate pattern marked by warmer-than-normal water temperatures in parts of the equatorial Pacific that emerges roughly every two to seven years. The changed ocean conditions can influence the atmosphere in ways that alter global weather patterns and change the distribution of rainfall, winds, tropical cyclones, fires, floods, and other phenomena. In the Bay of Bengal, for instance, some research indicates that altered environmental conditions during an El Niño are associated with a reduction in tropical cyclone activity. The ocean basin sees both less frequent and less intense tropical cyclones during El Niño years, researchers have found. NASA Earth Observatory image by Michala Garrison, using VIIRS day-night band data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE , GIBS/Worldview , and the Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS) . Story by Adam Voiland. item.title: Pushback over N70,000 allowance
item.description: By Idowu Isamotu, Daniel Adaji, Abuja & Abdullateef Aliyu, Lagos The leadership of the Trade Union Congress (TUC) on Wednesday rejected the federal government’s proposed six-month N70,000 transportation allowance for workers. The Congress, which described the government’s plan as a “haphazard measure” to cushion the effects of fuel subsidy removal, demanded an immediate salary increment for workers. Daily Trust reports that the government had on Tuesday approved a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants, beginning in November, to cushion the impact of rising living costs. The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a conciliation meeting between the federal government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday. This followed renewed pressure from organised labour over workers’ welfare, the rising cost of living and outstanding agreements. At the meeting, the government also approved the payment of outstanding peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. The meeting, which lasted several hours, witnessed a lot of disagreements and a series of back-and-forth, according to a senior labour leader who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity on Wednesday. “What we first demanded during the meeting was immediate reduction of the fuel price, but those on the government side opposed it. This led to disagreements for hours before the chief conciliator appealed to everyone. “After all the back-and-forth, the government side proposed N70,000 transport allowance for six months, not tagged wage award this time, and we reached a consensus on this,” the source said. Although the parties agreed to immediately constitute a Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee, they failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage. A memorandum of understanding signed at the end of the meeting, where the resolutions were contained, showed that leadership of the TUC was not part of the decision. Checks showed that the MoU was signed by the Director-General of Budget, Timi Yakubu; NLC President, Joe Ajaero; the Permanent Secretary, Service Welfare Office, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Dr Garba Abdul S.U. and the Minister of Labour and Employment, Maigari Dingyadi. TUC kicks The TUC argued that while it is good to negotiate minimum wage, which will affect other cadres of workers, the government must raise the wage level immediately. Speaking to journalists in Abuja shortly after rising from its National Administrative Council (NAC) meeting, the President of TUC, Festus Osifo, who was flanked by the General Secretary, Nuhu Toro, said there are no laws or historical practices stopping the government from doing so. He maintained that temporary wage awards are not sustainable, arguing that the wage award agreed on October 2, 2023 was to be implemented until a minimum wage was fixed in 2024 but was not enforced holistic

item.title: Caltech Names Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman as NASA JPL Deputy
item.description: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Former NASA astronaut and Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman joins Caltech and NASA JPL as Caltech associate vice president and JPL deputy director on Nov. 30. Photo Credit: NASA Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman has been named Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The emeritus astronaut and retired U.S. Navy captain begins his new role at NASA’s center of excellence for robotics and deep space exploration and at Caltech, which manages JPL for NASA, on Nov. 30, 2026. “Reid has spent his career at the edge of what is possible, and he has the technical judgment, operational experience, and leadership to help push that edge farther,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “As commander of Artemis II, he helped carry America back around the Moon, and now, as an emeritus astronaut, he will continue giving back to NASA from a new vantage point at JPL. Reid is joining a storied laboratory that has made an enormous amount of history, and there is a lot more ahead. I am excited to see what he and the JPL team accomplish in the years to come.” During the Artemis II test flight, Wiseman , Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen journeyed 695,081 miles on a lunar flyby that took them farther than any humans have ever traveled before. “It feels fitting for Reid, who with the Artemis II crew traveled farther from Earth than any human in history, to join Caltech and JPL — institutions that for nearly 90 years have sent spacecraft into the far reaches of our solar system and beyond,” said Dave Gallagher, JPL director and Caltech vice president. “Reid shares our drive for discovery, knows what it takes to lead teams through high-stakes missions, and has a remarkable ability to inspire people everywhere. He adds incredible bench strength to our leadership team as we build on the lab’s legacy and shape its future together.” After joining NASA’s astronaut corps in 2009, Wiseman went on to serve as flight engineer aboard the International Space Station for the 165-day Expedition 41 mission in 2014 and was a commander of NASA’s 21st Extreme Environment Mission Operations expedition, during which he lived for eight days in a habitat on the ocean floor in 2016. As the agency’s chief astronaut from December 2020 to November 2022, Wiseman led NASA’s astronaut corps, overseeing crew flight readiness and crew safety for all NASA human spaceflight missions. During his years of service at the agency, he has conducted hundreds of scientific experiments. “I’ve explored the furthest reaches of what a human can explore at NASA — and there were truly no words in the English vocabulary to describe seeing the Sun disappear behind the Moon from deep space. But that experience was really the jumping off point to go do the impossible things that Caltech and JPL dream, dare together, and do for NASA and the nation,” Wiseman s

item.title: IGP faces contempt for estate leader’s arrest despite pending court order
item.description: By Innocent Anaba The leadership of the GTHomes Estate Residents Association in Lekki area, Lagos, has initiated contempt proceeding against the Inspector General of Police, IGP, before a Federal High Court sitting in Lagos, over the arrest of the outgoing legal adviser of the association, Mr. Austin Akpomreta, despite a subsisting order for parties to maintain status quo. Akpomreta was arrested by members of the police from the Police Monitoring Unit, Abuja on Wednesday last week and whisked to Abuja, despite a pending court order. The arrest came weeks after reports emerged that the IGP had cautioned police formations against the misuse of police processes in matters with clear civil underpinnings and against practices that could encourage forum shopping by complainants dissatisfied with outcomes at other police formations. Akpomreta, who is one of the applicants in a suit pending before the Federal High Court, Lagos, was reportedly picked up on Wednesday morning despite a subsisting court order directing all parties to maintain the status quo pending the determination of the application before the court. He was said to be on his way to an unrelated court hearing when accosted by operatives of the Police Monitoring Unit and transported to Abuja. The arrest is reportedly in respect of the same dispute that is the subject of ongoing fundamental rights proceedings before the court, following disagreements relating to estate administration and utility services. The suit was instituted following concerns over repeated attempts by a resident, to use various police formations across Lagos and Abuja in relation to a dispute that multiple police commands and formations had reportedly regarded as civil in nature but was being framed as criminal, to invoke police involvement. All respondents in the matter, including the IGP, the Police Service Commission, and the investigating police officer in the matter, are said to have been duly served with the originating court processes as well as the order of the court directing parties to maintain the status quo pending the hearing and determination of the application. Akpomreta wife, Faith, said her husband’s arrest while the court order remains in force, “raises serious questions about compliance with judicial processes. and respect for the authority of the court.” The applicants have consistently maintained that the issues in dispute are civil in nature and are properly suited for determination by a court of competent jurisdiction and are urging all institutions and parties connected with the matter to respect the authority of the Federal High Court and allow the judicial process to run its course without intimidation, harassment, or actions capable of rendering the court proceedings nugatory. item.title: Google struggling to make AI Mode searches pay
item.description: Shares in Google’s parent company Alphabet dived by almost ten percent on Wednesday, after the web giant admitted AI-powered searches earn it less money than it earns by serving ads with its old-school search engine. Alphabet on Wednesday reported its Q3 results, which included news that its year-over-year search query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years. Some of that growth comes from users adopting “AI Mode” – Google’s latest LLM-powered search system. Google’s revenue from search rose 12 percent year-over-year to $63.25 billion, a little lower than the 14.5 percent growth the company reported in last year’s Q3. During Alphabet’s earnings call, chief business officer Philipp Schindler said the slowdown was caused by “lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode.” That’s a worry given that Google is spending enormous sums on infrastructure. $51.4 billion went out the door in Q3, around two thirds of it going towards servers and networking equipment. The rest funded datacenter builds. That spending appears to have impacted profitability, as Alphabet reported $26.17 billion net income for the quarter. Last year’s Q3, during which Google revenue was $102.35 billion, produced $35 billion net income. Schindler argued that AI search will pay off. “On AI Mode, many of these queries are upper funnel queries, allowing us to capture new, high-value commercial intent,” he told investors. “In addition, the majority of AI Mode queries are incremental, creating more monetization opportunities over time.” Google tried to seize one of those opportunities today, by turning on ads alongside AI Mode searches around the world, after first testing them in the US only. But for now, AI Mode searches aren’t as lucrative as Google’s existing search business, which brought in just under half of Alphabet's $125.8 billion quarterly revenue. Google’s cloud is its next-best earner, at $24.75 billion for the quarter, but it has troubles too because the Big G doesn’t have enough capacity to serve all its customers. The company has started to offload some customer workloads to third parties, and warned that will dent its future margins. Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud’s CEO, said the company has over 100 companies using its TPU silicon, adding that “All of the inventory for TPU systems are associated with committed contracts” – meaning Google can see some revenue to cover some capex. The company expects to book revenue from TPU sales to third parties in coming quarters. CEO Sundar Pichai was full of optimism for future AI revenue, noting that Google’s Gemini app has won a billion users faster than any other product in the company’s history, and praising the performance of its models. He said Google is moving fast to create agentic AI tools, but will focus on business customers for starters, “because the bar for security, safety, and governance is extremely high.” “As a next step, we are bringing these features to Search and also, of course, to our billion us

item.title: AU accredits Nigeria’s counter-terrorism centre for West Africa
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The African Union (AU) has accredited Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), under the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), as a Regional Centre of Excellence in Counter Terrorism for West Africa and the Sahel. The accreditation fulfils President Bola Tinubu’s vision, announced at the High-Level African Counter Terrorism Meeting held in Abuja in April 2024, to position the NCTC as a regional hub for intelligence sharing, operational coordination, specialised training and capacity building against terrorism and violent extremism. A statement issued on Thursday by Abu Michael, Head of Strategic Communication at the NCTC, said the designation marked a significant milestone in Nigeria’s contribution to collective African security. It said the recognition formally positioned the centre to support AU member states, particularly those in West Africa and the Sahel, through enhanced counter-terrorism cooperation and institutional capacity development. According to the statement, the accreditation gives the NCTC an expanded regional mandate to provide specialised training, joint threat analysis, research, technical assistance, exchanges of lessons learned and other forms of counter-terrorism support. The accreditation was announced on October 27, 2026, by the Acting Director of the African Union Counter Terrorism Centre (AUCTC), Dr Idriss Mounir Lallali, on behalf of the AU Commission’s Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security, at the conclusion of the African Lessons Learned Forum in Abuja. Lallali said the recognition followed a rigorous assessment of the NCTC’s institutional capacity, governance, training programmes, analytical capabilities, coordination mechanisms and adherence to human rights and the rule of law. He explained that the accreditation process began with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the AU and the NCTC in September 2025. This was followed by a technical assessment mission conducted by the AUCTC in Abuja in December 2025, which produced an accreditation roadmap outlining the institutional standards required for recognition. Since then, the NCTC has worked to strengthen its governance structures, develop training curricula and operational procedures, improve its analytical and coordination functions, and reinforce its commitment to human rights and the rule of law. The statement said the successful completion of the accreditation requirements reflected the centre’s institutional development and the collaborative efforts of ONSA, NCTC leadership and personnel, as well as strategic partners. Announcing the decision, Lallali said: “It is therefore my pleasure to announce that the African Union is accrediting the NCTC as an African Union Regional Centre of Excellence in Counter Terrorism. “This decision will be conveyed formally to the Government of the Federal Republic of Nigeria through a Note Verbale. item.title: ALTON urges states to scrap telecoms right-of-way fees
item.description: Association says charges account for up to 60% of fibre deployment costs By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) has urged state governments to abolish right-of-way charges on telecommunications infrastructure, warning that the fees account for up to 60 per cent of fibre-optic deployment costs in some states and discourage network expansion into underserved communities. The association said scrapping the charges, particularly in rural areas and locations with limited commercial prospects, would lower infrastructure deployment costs, attract investment and help bridge Nigeria’s digital divide. ALTON Chairman, Engr. Gbenga Adebayo, made the call on Tuesday on the sidelines of a plenary session sponsored by IHS Nigeria at the 2026 Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja. Right-of-way charges are fees imposed for permission to access and use public or private land, roads and other designated spaces to install fibre-optic cables and related telecommunications infrastructure. Adebayo said the high cost of obtaining right-of-way approvals had become a major obstacle to fibre deployment, making it difficult for operators to justify investments in communities where anticipated revenue might not cover infrastructure costs. “Today, the cost of right-of-way amounts to a significant part of the cost of fibre deployment. For every one kilometre of fibre that you deploy, in some of the states, the cost of right-of-way can be as high as 50 to 60 per cent of the cost of deploying the entire infrastructure,” he said. He called for legislation to make right-of-way access for telecommunications infrastructure free, particularly in rural communities and other areas where expected commercial returns were unlikely to attract private investment. According to him, removing the charges would make network expansion more affordable and encourage operators to extend services to communities with poor or no connectivity. The ALTON chairman also urged the government to introduce incentives for telecommunications companies investing in areas where infrastructure deployment costs exceeded the revenue they could reasonably expect to generate. He said existing government intervention mechanisms, particularly the Universal Service Provision Fund (USPF), could be deployed more strategically to support network expansion in underserved locations. “There are also intervention funds. We have the Universal Service Provision Fund, which is designed for special intervention in those areas that are lacking coverage,” Adebayo said. He dismissed suggestions that telecommunications operators were unwilling to invest in rural communities, arguing that the challenge was largely economic and could be addressed through appropriate incentives and targeted government support. Beyond expanding network coverage, Adebayo stressed the need for increased investment in fibre-optic cables, telecommunications sites and network capacity to improve servic

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 28, 1971: Britain launches its 1st satellite Prospero into space on a Black Arrow rocket
item.description: null On Oct. 28, 1971, the United Kingdom launched its first satellite. The satellite was named Prospero, but it was also known as the X-3. This wasn't Britain's first satellite , but it was the first and only one the British space program launched with one of its own rockets. The first six British satellites all launched from the United States on NASA rockets. Prospero launched on a carrier rocket called the Black Arrow. The Prospero mission was the fourth and final flight of a Black Arrow rocket . Prospero was designed to study how the environment in space affects communications satellites. It tested things solar cells and telemetry systems, and even had a micrometeoroid detector that would determine small particles in space posed a threat to the spacecraft. The mission lifted off from the Woomera Range Complex in Australia. While the launch was a success, the rocket's final stage bumped into the satellite after it separated, and the collision broke one of Prospero's four radio antennas. But the satellite still worked, and it remained operational until 1973. The satellite Prospero X-3 is launched from the RAAF test range in Woomera, South Australia, by a British Black Arrow carrier rocket, 28th October 1971. Central Press/Hulton Archive/Getty Images Britain developed the Black Arrow as its national satellite launcher. Based on the smaller Black Knight research rocket this was a three-stage vehicle, 12.87m tall. SSPL/Getty Images Why it mattered The launch of Prospero is etched in the history books of British spaceflight. To this date, it remains the first and last British satellite ever launched on a native rocket built in the United Kingdom. The 66-kilogram satellite launched on a three-stage Black Arrow R-3 rocket and flew in an elliptical orbit that ranged between 522 km to 1,300 km above the Earth. The rocket itself was based on the smaller Black Knight research rocket and stood nearly 13 meters tall. While the launch was successful, the Black Arrow program, which had seen two failures and two successes, was ultimately canceled. The research satellite Prospero is the only British spacecraft to launch on the British-built Black Arrow rocket. (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons/Geni) The Prospero satellite, meanwhile, operated in orbit for two years, with regular communications ending in 1973, though it was contacted at least once each year through 1996, according to the BBC . The satellite remains in orbit today, its legacy such that at least one company - the Scotland-based space startup Skyrora, has announced plans to retrieve Prospero in orbit and deorbit in Earth's atmosphere. That Skyrora plan, announced in 2021 , would use the company's space tug to rendezvous with the defunct Prospero, latch onto it and pull it from space. The company aims to launch its Skyrora XL rocket out of a Saxavord Spaceport in Scotland. "By recovering Prospero, we are not only coming together as a space nation and taking responsibility for what we have launched i

item.title: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
item.description: United Launch Alliance announced Wednesday it plans to return its Vulcan rocket to service on November 13, nine months after a solid rocket booster anomaly threw the company's 2026 launch schedule into oblivion. The return-to-flight mission will launch 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network. The mission will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, and ULA said the launch date is pending range approval. The launch is critical for ULA after its new flagship rocket suffered nozzle failures on its solid rocket boosters on two of its first four missions, most recently during a flight in February. In both cases, the rocket overcame the nozzle failure and completed its mission, but officials at the US Space Force, ULA's primary customer, lost confidence in Vulcan. Read full article Comments

item.description: The European Union plans to create the first subsea Internet cable directly connecting Europe to Greenland. The Pan-Arctic Cable project could also extend to Canada and eventually link with Japan and South Korea, notably bypassing the United States. The Pan-Arctic Cable is described as a European Union flagship project in a European Commission joint communication published on October 20, 2026. The policy document describes a new European strategy for the Arctic that supports “a sovereign, secure and resilient submarine cable connection linking Greenland directly to the EU,” while also suggesting that “like-minded partners like Canada” could provide a stepping stone for future cable expansion toward Asia. “It is interesting that this project is even being considered, because five years ago it would have seemed like not a particularly commercially attractive proposition,” Elisabeth Braw , a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council who leads the Threats to the Global Maritime Order Initiative, told Ars. “But the fact that it's being considered is very much on trend and a sign of our times.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea in League Cup shoot-out, Man City survive scare
item.description: Liverpool beat Chelsea in a dramatic penalty shoot-out to reach the League Cup quarter-finals, while holders Manchester City survived a scare against Brighton on Wednesday. In a clash between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso, it was the Liverpool manager who took the bragging rights in the last-16 tie at Anfield. A 1-1 draw in normal time set the stage for the shoot-out as Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers netted from the spot, only for Cody Gakpo to equalise with a penalty of his own just before half-time. Chelsea’s Valentin Barco hit the post in the shoot-out before Liverpool’s Kostas Tsimikas wasted a chance to win it when he blazed over. Ryan Gravenberch was denied by Chelsea keeper Mike Penders, but Giorgi Mamardashvili saved Emmanuel Emegha’s kick to keep Liverpool alive. After Joe Gomez scored for Liverpool, Blues defender Wesley Fofana miscued into the Kop as the hosts advanced. It was former Liverpool midfielder Alonso’s third defeat in his three visits to Anfield as a manager following losses with Bayer Leverkusen in 2024 and Real Madrid in 2025. In their debut campaigns at Liverpool, Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot both reached the League Cup final and Iraola is on course to follow in their footsteps with the 10-time winners of the competition. Alonso made just four changes to the Chelsea side that lost 2-0 at home to Tottenham on Saturday, while Iraola made seven changes from Liverpool’s 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday. Rogers put Chelsea in front with a 40th-minute penalty after Gravenberch clattered into Moises Caicedo. But Liverpool were level three minutes later with a penalty of their own as Gakpo converted from the spot following Fofana’s handball. At the Etihad Stadium, City were pushed to the brink by Brighton in a 2-2 draw before winning on penalties. City boss Enzo Maresca made nine changes after Saturday’s loss at Aston Villa — which ended the leaders’ 100 percent start to the Premier League campaign. – Rulli stars for City – Erling Haaland, Ruben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Gianluigi Donnarumma were among the City stars rested. Brighton went in front after 30 minutes when Malick Yalcouye steered Georginio Rutter’s shot past Geronimo Rulli from five yards. Mateo Kovacic hauled City level 20 minutes later with a fine finish that curled into the far corner from 25 yards. Rutter restored Brighton’s lead two minutes after half-time, slotting home from Jaouen Hadjam’s cut-back. Vitor Reis deflected in Rayan Cherki’s 72nd-minute free-kick to equalise for City. Kovacic’s penalty was saved by Jason Steele in the shoot-out, but Rulli denied Brighton’s Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight. The sides meet again in the Premier League at the Etihad on Saturday. Bournemouth extended their blistering run with a 3-0 win against Aston Villa at the Vitality Stadium. item.title: Ballon d’Or winner Kane watches as Bayern cruise into German Cup last 16
item.description: Newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was left on the bench as Bayern Munich sailed to a 6-1 win over second-tier Magdeburg in the German Cup last 32 on Wednesday. Bayern had no difficulty without their star striker, with Michael Olise grabbing a double and Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies, Nathaniel Brown and teenager David Santos Daiber also getting on the scoresheet. Kane received a guard of honour from his Bayern teammates before kick-off as the 75,000 fans at the Allianz Arena saluted the Ballon d’Or winner, two days after his triumph in London. Bayern got some more good news pre-match, with coach Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital, five days after collapsing at training on Friday. “We’re also winning for him of course,” Brown said of Kompany. “It’s really good that he’s back home now. He should get some rest, but hopefully we’ll see him again soon.” Olise tapped in an excellent Saibari assist from close range after 10 minutes but the unfancied visitors levelled five minutes later through Mateusz Zukowski. Olise returned the favour by setting up Saibari midway through the opening half and added a third from the spot early in the second half before smiling and pointing to Kane, Bayern’s regular penalty taker, on the bench. Teenage forward Lennart Karl set up goals for Davies and Brown before Santos Daiber added more gloss to the victory with a stoppage-time goal. Kane remained on the bench for the entire match, with Saturday’s home Bundesliga clash with Borussia Dortmund in mind. Bayer Leverkusen came from two goals down to win 5-2 against Nuremberg, with defender Edmond Tapsoba netting twice and Patrik Schick, Jonas Hofmann and Lucas Vazquez scoring goals. Earlier on Wednesday, Germany forward Deniz Undav’s 90th-minute strike took Stuttgart to a 1-0 win at 10-man Paderborn. Stuttgart, finalists in 2025, had a one-man advantage after Laurin Curda’s 37th-minute red card but could not break down a stubborn Paderborn. After striker Ermedin Demirovic had two efforts saved, Undav took matters into his own hands and turned in a Chris Fuehrich cross with extra time looming. “The win is what matters most,” Undav said. “I honestly don’t care whether I’m the one who scores, and that’s the truth. We won, we’re through to the next round — on we go.” Japan forward Keisuke Goto scored twice in the final 15 minutes to overturn a 2-1 deficit as Freiburg won 3-2 at home against Wolfsburg. Goto’s Japan teammate Kento Shiogai also bagged a brace, while Freiburg’s Igor Matanovic opened the scoring. Elsewhere, second-division sides Dynamo Dresden and Hertha Berlin both won 2-0 against Schalke and Jeddeloh respectively, while Kaiserslautern eliminated Hannover. AFP The post Ballon d’Or winner Kane watches as Bayern cruise into German Cup last 16 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Peptide peddlers cheer as RFK Jr. unilaterally grants access, overruling FDA
item.description: Anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy has unilaterally passed a rule that will allow specialty pharmacies to sell six specific peptide drugs, overruling scientists at the Food and Drug Administration. The peptides are popular among members of Kennedy's Make America Health Again movement and many prominent MAHA figures and Kennedy allies sell them. Kennedy said he uses some of the peptides and called himself a "big fan." But FDA scientists continue to say there is insufficient evidence to show if they're effective and they are potentially dangerous. In 2023, the safety concerns led the FDA to remove the six peptides from a list of drugs that can be made by specialty pharmacies called compounding pharmacies—which make customized formulations of drugs for patients, or, in cases such as this, specialty drugs in bulk. Kennedy's new rule sidesteps the need to formally undo that FDA action. The rule is titled "Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances" and was made available Wednesday on the Federal Register , with the final publication data set for October 30. The rule does not change the regulatory status of the peptide; instead, it states the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will no longer take enforcement action against compounding pharmacies for making the peptides, essentially giving them a green light to freely produce and sell them. Kennedy had quietly proposed this rule earlier this month. Read full article Comments

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil's true leader after fleeing to US
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country's rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile. Bolsonaro's defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Fabio de Sa e Silva, Associate Professor of International Studies at the University of Oklahoma. He says that an attempt by Bolsonaro to turn a domestic dispute into a wider international issue "will not be successful", explaining that he is likely going to be "losing the grip of the opposition, there is a vacuum now that others will seek to occupy" and that it's unlikely that the United States will "get involved into questioning the results of the Brazilian election".

item.title: Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to US
item.description: Brazil’s defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country’s rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile. Bolsonaro’s defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday. “I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Bolsonaro said in the statement published on his X account, slamming “electoral fraud.” “I will lead the opposition from here,” he said. In a subsequent statement, he revised his claim, saying he is the “leader,” rather than “president.” Bolsonaro, 45, touched down earlier Wednesday in a private jet at Opa-Locka Executive Airport near Miami. President Donald Trump’s hard-right administration has strong links to Bolsonaro and his father Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brazil after attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022. Trump reiterated his stand that Brazil’s election was “very strange” but told reporters he “won’t get involved” in Flavio Bolsonaro’s claim to the presidency. Details of how Bolsonaro, accompanied by his wife and daughters, made it to US soil are still emerging. He is under investigation in his home country over alleged corruption and money laundering. With his current parliamentary immunity about to expire, he was ordered to surrender his passports but left anyway, reaching the United States via Argentina and Ecuador. A police source told AFP that Bolsonaro’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, but the senator has also held Italian nationality since 2023, according to Italian documents seen by AFP. The US Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that the Bolsonaro family members were inspected and cleared “with applicable immigration laws and procedures.” The travel ban was issued by powerful Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who led the case against Flavio Bolsonaro’s father and is a controversial figure hated by the Brazilian right. Flavio Bolsonaro had vowed to seek the justice’s impeachment if he were elected — which up until Lula’s comeback in the runoff had looked increasingly likely. – ‘Shameful’ act – Lula, who won the election with 51.8 percent of Sunday’s vote, called Flavio Bolsonaro’s departure a “shameful” act. “A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide,” he said in Brasilia during his 81st birthday celebration on Tuesday. But Brazil police issued a statement Wednesday saying that he was not considered a fugitive. There was controversy in neighboring Argentina, where opposition lawmakers demanded to know how Bolsonaro had managed to transit through the country. While Argentinian authorities said he was carrying valid travel documents, officials have requested chief of cabinet Diego Santilli to provide details to parliamen

item.title: Solid Minerals: FG Inaugurates Nigeria-US Committee On Strategic Cooperation
item.description: The Federal Government has inaugurated the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja to advance the partnership with the US. This came weeks after the Federal Government and the United States of America signed a memorandum of understanding to boost the development of Nigeria’s solid minerals sector. The agreement was signed on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly between Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US Deputy Secretary of State, Christopher Landau, at the Nigerian Mission House in New York, United States. The minister, who inaugurated the committee, however, refuted claims that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to America. “I inaugurated the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja to advance our partnership with the United States and set the record straight on reports claiming Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to America,” Alake stated in a post on X. “Let me be very clear. Nigeria has not sold its mineral assets.” He explained that the agreement signed with the US was a government-to-government framework designed to connect American investors with Nigerian businesses. “It is about attracting investment, sharing technology, expanding local processing and creating jobs. “Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s leadership, we are determined to move beyond an economy heavily dependent on oil,” he said. The minister stated that Nigeria’s mineral resources must create greater value at home and deliver lasting benefits to Nigerians. “That is why local processing is now a key requirement for investors seeking mineral titles. “Our partnership with the US offers an opportunity to match Nigeria’s vast resources with the capital and technology needed to build a stronger mining industry. The progress we are seeing in mineral processing reflects this direction,” he added. Alake urged the committee to approach the responsibility with diligence, identify viable investment opportunities and turn the agreement into measurable results that support President Tinubu’s $1 trillion economy target. According to him, the focus is ensuring that Nigeria’s mineral wealth creates jobs, strengthens our economy and delivers real value to our people. At the signing of the MoU in September , the minister had said that the implementation would achieve the economic diversification goals of the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu and boost industrial growth. Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau, at the Nigerian Mission House in New York, United States, during the pact signing. The Deputy Secretary of State Landau was quoted as expressing strong agreement with Nigeria’s position, adding that as Africa’s fastest-growing economy and most populous country, Nigeria is a regional power that deserves partnership with the US.

item.title: No ministers paid billions for appointments, APC insists
item.description: By Dickson Omobola The All Progressives Congress, APC, Wednesday, denied claims that ministers pay billions of Naira to secure appointments, saying comments made by its Presidential Campaign Council spokesperson, Alwan Hassan, referred to historical practices rather than the current administration. Hassan had alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and subsequently seek to recover the money. Speaking during an interview on Arise TV, Hassan said: “The way Asiwaju is hands-on on the expenditure of our revenue is fantastic and I love it. A lot of ministers pay billions and billions, and, you know, to get themselves appointed. The first thing they think of is how to recoup that money.” Reacting to the statement, which has generated backlash, National Publicity Secretary of APC, Felix Morka, questioned how ministers who allegedly paid billions to secure appointments would recover such sums within Nigeria’s budgetary framework. Speaking on Primetime, an Arise TV programme, Morka said Hassan had explained that his remarks were not directed at the current administration but were made in a historical context. His words: “What he was referring to was not really about this administration, but he was speaking in historical context. What he said left a lot of ambiguity, some have suggested that he was speaking about appointments. He was clear as well when he said that what he was describing predated APC. As a citizen listening to him, I thought he was simply conflating systems. When he came back and said it predated the APC, that suggested to me that his frame of thought was really located, not in the present, but really in the past. “When you are a public commentator, sometimes you generalise without really specifically drawing those lines of distinction between moments. If I say there’s corruption in Nigeria, I’m not necessarily saying that this government is corrupt. am not here to sort of overanalyse or justify comments. I think that, in due time, he alone will have to come tell what he had in his mind. But from talking to him, what I understood, after the fact, was that he was simply speaking historically, to say that ministers generally in our country have had this really terrible record of engaging in that behaviour. “If ministers are paying billions to get appointed, how exactly, within what we know to be Nigeria’s budgetary frame, do you recoup the billions you paid to get appointed? I don’t think that is really something that, personally, I am willing to even imagine. He made a comment in historical context, as he explained it. In other democracies, lobbying for appointments is not something unusual. In the United States, there are firms that are contracted to lobby for individuals to get appointed to office. Those are usual things that happen in the background.prior to appointments. “I think the concern here is that when lobbying becomes monetised, where people pay money to operators or to individuals with influence

item.title: 2027: Kwankwaso warns INEC over alleged AI-generated images in voter register
item.description: ‎ ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎Former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has warned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) that alleged irregularities in the preliminary voter register could undermine the credibility of the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso raised the concern in a statement posted on his official Facebook page, following reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other questionable records in the register. ‎ ‎He warned that failure to properly investigate the allegations could weaken public confidence in Nigeria’s electoral system ahead of the elections. ‎ ‎According to him, the development raises serious questions about the integrity of the voter registration process and the measures put in place by INEC to prevent electoral manipulation. ‎ ‎”With the 2027 elections approaching, INEC must provide Nigerians with clear and convincing answers,” he said. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso questioned how the suspicious photographs found their way into the register, whether the individuals involved were genuinely registered and if their identities were properly verified. ‎ ‎While welcoming INEC’s decision to investigate the allegations, the former governor insisted that Nigerians deserved more than assurances from the electoral body. ‎ ‎He called for a thorough, transparent and independent investigation, saying the findings must be made public and anyone found responsible held accountable under the law. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso also demanded a comprehensive independent audit of the preliminary voter register to identify questionable entries, duplicate registrations and possible artificial identities. ‎ ‎He, however, stressed that the exercise must not deny eligible Nigerians their constitutional right to vote. ‎ ‎”Our democracy cannot afford any compromise in the integrity of the voter register. Every eligible Nigerian must have the right to vote, and every vote must count,” he said. ‎ ‎The former governor further warned against the use of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, to manipulate the electoral process. ‎ ‎”Nobody should be allowed to exploit technology, including artificial intelligence, to undermine our electoral system,” he added. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso maintained that the credibility of the 2027 general elections would depend largely on the accuracy and integrity of the voter register. ‎ ‎”The credibility of the 2027 elections begins with a credible voter register, and INEC must get its act together,” he declared The post 2027: Kwankwaso warns INEC over alleged AI-generated images in voter register appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 5 days beneath the waves: What it's like to live in an underwater 'space station'
item.description:
Dr. Michaela Musilova is an award-winning astrobiologist, explorer, professional speaker and author. Michaela has been conducting space-related research at institutions around the world, including NASA, ESA, CalTech, the Canada-France-Hawaii telescope and many others. She was the Commander of 40 simulated missions to the Moon and Mars — the most missions led to date.

Currently, Michaela is the President and Founder of the nonprofit XtremeFrontiers. She is pioneering a unique global project: Astro Seven Summits. It's a world-first in combining expeditions to the highest mountain on each continent with scientific research in collaboration with NASA and institutions worldwide, educational activities and filming documentaries.

Michaela is also a consultant for numerous companies across the globe for topics ranging from Mars missions all the way to museum exhibitions, such as for the Smithsonian. She is one of very few people to have ever led research projects on all seven continents.

Michaela’s work has been recognized through numerous awards, such as Forbes 30 Under 30, Top 100 Women in Aerospace and Aviation, and the Emerging Space Leaders Grant.

Michaela is regularly invited to give keynote presentations and performs a variety of outreach activities globally as a science communicator. She has been giving interviews to international media for over 20 years, writing scientific and educational articles, and she co-authored her biography, "Woman from Mars."

Living underwater was surprisingly peaceful. It was in many ways exactly what I imagine living on Mars would be like one day. There were no humans around us, except for my three SEA STAR crewmembers and me. Apart from the human noises we made, we couldn't hear anything other than the life support systems keeping us alive submerged 22 feet (7 meters) below the surface. We were living in these extreme conditions to study the challenges astronauts may face on long-duration space missions. Since performing research in space is still rare and expensive, there are numerous facilities around the world that focus on recreating space-like conditions on Earth . One of those stations is the Jules' Undersea Lab, where the SEA STAR simulated space mission took place. This underwater habitat was called "La Chalupa" when it was built in the 1970s. Its purpose was to allow divers to live and perform research as aquanauts — people who spend more than 24 hours underwater in a so-called state of saturation. Today, the Jules' Undersea Lab is located near Key Largo, in Florida. However, it was originally designed to be mobile — inside a barge 20 feet wide and 60 feet long (6 to 18 meters). The SEA STAR crew inside the Jules' Undersea Lab, as seen from the outside of the station by a member of Mission Control. (Image credit: Ozlem Berg) The aquanauts could choose an ideal site for their research expeditions underwater and then have the facility be submerged. They did

item.title: Chelsea Win As Bayern, Madrid Share Points In Women’s Champions League
item.description: Goals from Ellie Carpenter and Kadeisha Buchanan were enough to secure a second win for Chelsea in this season’s Women’s Champions League on Wednesday, while Bayern Munich came from two goals down to draw with Real Madrid. Chelsea, who reached the final in 2020-21, opened their campaign with a win and a draw despite scoring just once in their first two games. They looked nailed on for another win in the first half at Plough Lane as they dominated the game without getting a goal. Alyssa Thompson hit the crossbar while Aggie Beever-Jones, put away by a superb pass from Hannah Hampton, was denied by a last-ditch challenge from Shukurat Oladipo. That changed in the 51st minute when Wieke Kaptein cut the ball back for substitute Carpenter, making her 50th Champions League appearance, who slid the ball under the goalkeeper Rachele Baldi. Melvine Malard missed a golden chance to put the game to bed, but Buchanan sealed it a minute from time, heading Kaptein’s cross into the Roma net. Bayern Munich’s Spanish forward Edna Imade (R) celebrates scoring the 1-2 goal with her teammates during the UEFA Women’s Champions League – League phase, Matchday 3 – football match between FC Bayern Munich and Real Madrid in Unterhaching near Munich, southern Germany, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) There was a moment’s silence before kick-off at the Sportpark Unterhaching in Munich as a mark of respect after at least 68 people were killed in a train crash near Madrid earlier on Wednesday. Real Madrid, who were all wearing black armbands, took an early lead when Athenea found the net in the seventh minute. They doubled their lead 15 minutes later when former Bayern forward Lineth Beerensteyn headed home from close range, her first goal for Madrid in the Champions League since her move in the summer. Real Madrid’s Spanish forward Athenea del Castillo (C) celebrates scoring the opening goal with her teammates during the UEFA Women’s Champions League – League phase, Matchday 3 – football match between FC Bayern Munich and Real Madrid in Unterhaching near Munich, southern Germany, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) / ALTERNATIVE CROP Bayern hit back shortly after when Edna Imade met Klara Buhl’s corner from the left and powered her header into the net. And they drew level in the 52nd minute when Momoko Tanikawa curled in from the edge of the box after Madrid keeper Merle Frohms parried out a shot from Linda Dallmann. Swiss side Servette dispatched Belgium’s OH Leuven 5-1 with Paola Hernandez and Gloria Marinelli scoring two goals each. Wednesday’s late matches see Arsenal host Benfica while eight-time winners Lyon are at home to Inter Milan. AFP The post Chelsea Win As Bayern, Madrid Share Points In Women’s Champions League appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Please state the nature of the medical emergency: Google is building a robot medic for NASA
item.description: Google is working with NASA to develop a robotic medical assistant that could help astronauts on future deep-space missions. Chocolate Factory's public sector VP Jim Kelly said in a Tuesday blog post that the company's latest moonshot could take its technology far beyond the lunar surface, with Google's public sector arm partnering with NASA's Human Research Program, Johnson Space Center's robotics team, and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory to develop a robot that could assist astronauts with medical tasks, cargo handling, and routine maintenance. The robotics project builds on the Crew Medical Officer Digital Assistant (CMO-DA), an AI-powered medical decision-support system Google has been working on with NASA since last year. CMO-DA, which is powered by the Red Hat-supported open source local AI tool RamaLama, is already being evaluated on Earth-bound copies of computers used aboard the ISS. It’s designed to run AI models locally for evaluation of medical issues, which will be a key part of future space missions due to the communications lag between Earth and astronauts in deep space. “An astronaut on a future deep space mission to Mars could face severe operational challenges—including round-trip communication latencies of up to 44 minutes, making real-time medical guidance for crew nearly impossible,” Kelly said in this week’s blog post. Google and NASA envision the robot as an assistant to a human crew medical officer, helping with medical tasks and doing other work when bedside assistance isn't required. “To maximize its utility for a lean crew, the robotic system is designed as a versatile 'payload' handler capable of managing cargo, logistics, and equipment,” Kelly explained. “When not needed for routine maintenance like organizing tools or securing compartments, it can pivot to medical support.” As one example of its potential use, the Google public sector VP explained that, were someone to experience severe back pain potentially caused by kidney stones, the robot could fetch and prep an ultrasound machine, leaving the crew medical officer to interpret the scan and decide on treatment. “The ultimate goal is to build a robotic system that can execute a variety of tasks via simple voice instructions, under the astronauts’ direct supervision and command,” Kelly said. “For instance, the robot might be directed to assist with routine health monitoring—such as capturing basic vitals or simple ultrasounds—under the strict guidance of a human crew medical officer.” So, not a full-fledged digital medical officer as much as an extra set of hands for an overworked human doc. As for the status of the project, it doesn't appear to have advanced too far yet. Google outlines several technologies being explored, including JPL's work adapting satellite situational-awareness tools originally used to track objects in orbit to help the robot navigate 3D spaces. item.title: S.E.A CONSULTING Showcases Nigerian Craftsmanship at Design Week Lagos 2026
item.description: At this year’s Design Week Lagos , S.EA.CONSULTING brought its vision to REDESIGN AFRICA to life through an interactive exhibition that invited visitors to touch, listen, explore and connect. Presented at the National Theatre, Lagos, the installation placed local craftsmanship at the centre of a contemporary African living experience. Deep burgundy surfaces, raw tree bark, sculptural textures and a contemporary sofa from S.EA.HOMES created a setting shaped by Nigerian culture and heritage. Finishing materials were served on a dark hardwood table supported by clear acrylic bases, giving the illusion of floating wood. Guests could handle samples and discover the possibilities behind the finished spaces. Wireless headphones offered a choice of music and the founder’s statement, while a digital screen introduced the firm’s services, products, and projects. An in-house photographer captured visitors engaging with the installation, making their presence part of its story. Through this approach, S.EA.CONSULTING made a clear statement: African exhibitions should give local makers, materials and ways of living a central role. Cultural heritage offers a foundation for contemporary design that meets global standards of quality, functionality and execution. The experience connected interior architecture with sourcing, craftsmanship and everyday life, demonstrating how collaboration transforms individual products into spaces with meaning. For S.EA.CONSULTING, showing the world how we live begins with recognising the value of what we make, the stories we carry and the hands that bring our ideas to life. Rooted in culture. Built through collaboration. REDESIGN AFRICA. item.title: Atiku challenges Tinubu to prove he’s in Makkah
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide daily proof of his presence in Makkah for Umrah, alleging that the planned pilgrimage could be a smokescreen for a trip to France. Atiku said Nigerians deserved to know the President’s actual destination, daily engagements and the purpose of the trip, raising questions about a reported $20 billion loan request involving a French business partner. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said intelligence available to him suggested that Tinubu might make only a brief appearance in Makkah before proceeding to France. He called on the Presidency to release clear, current and date-stamped photographs and videos each day showing Tinubu at the Kaaba and performing the rites of Umrah. “Nigerians deserve verifiable proof of the President’s presence in Makkah and a transparent account of his daily activities in the Holy Land,” he said. Atiku also questioned whether the trip was connected to the President’s health and the reported $20 billion loan request, urging the Presidency to address the concerns and disclose the full itinerary. The former vice president said he and other Nigerians would join Tinubu in prayers for the country’s peace and progress, but warned against invoking religion without sincerity. “No one should invoke the name of Almighty Allah in vain,” he said, insisting that a spiritual mission undertaken on behalf of the nation must be treated with seriousness and transparency. He maintained that Nigerians were entitled to know how the trip was being funded and demanded verifiable evidence of the President’s whereabouts and activities. The post Atiku challenges Tinubu to prove he’s in Makkah appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Anthropic engineer declares the coding interview dead
item.description: Why ask a human to complete a coding test when they can just use an AI to help them? Anthropic engineering manager Felix Rieseberg says he has stopped using traditional coding interviews for his team. "Being able to quickly define problems and find elegant solutions was a weak but useful predictor for how successful you’d be on my teams," Rieseberg explained in a blog post on Tuesday. "Small coding challenges in real code did tell us something meaningful about candidates." No longer, he says. The coding interview is dead , as far as he's concerned. "There’s no more point in giving you a little React challenge than there is in quizzing people about assembly; Claude is now better at both," he insisted. "Our most impactful builders are successful regardless of how good they are at these tests." In a response posted to social media, Jaana Dogan, principal engineer at Google, said much the same. "I’m not doing a ton of coding interviews nowadays but I’d be interested to interview how people use coding agents," she wrote . "That itself gives me more signals about candidates' coding skills." Several months ago, Google reportedly began reevaluating how it conducts coding interviews and what it looks for in candidates. And while it would be surprising if similar conversations haven't already occurred at other large technology companies where AI agents have demonstrated their coding capabilities, the rest of the tech industry appears to be moving more cautiously than the AI enthusiasts. "We are not seeing tech companies abandon skills assessments widely across the industry—at least not yet," said Nicole Bachaud, labor economist at ZipRecruiter, in an email to The Register . "In fact, based on our October 2026 Employer Survey of 1,500 employers, we see the tech industry (Information sector specifically) is actually the most likely to test for skills, with 62.5 percent of employers requiring formal skill tests on initial applications." Coding interviews at Microsoft, and later Google, Amazon, Facebook, and other tech giants, vary, depending on what the hiring organization aims to evaluate. They may probe technical knowledge related to a specific subject, coding ability in a particular language, general problem-solving skills, team-oriented behavior, or other skills. Stripe's software engineer interview process, according to Educative , consists of a phone screening stage, a technical phone interview, and several further on-site interviews. Rieseberg actually worked there and describes how founder Patrick Collison urged new hires to pay attention to things that seemed out of place. "His bet was that newcomers would spot friction and opportunities that old-timers had long stopped noticing," he said. item.title: Natural resources not enough for national prosperity – Makinde
item.description: Gov. Seyi Makinde said natural resources alone cannot guarantee a prosperous national economy. Makinde stated this on Wednesday at the 10th anniversary celebration and inauguration of the CapitalSage Holdings Global Headquarters in Ibadan According to the governor, sustainable growth depends on entrepreneurship, skills, knowledge and intensive production. He noted that while Nigeria is richly endowed with natural resources, sustainable economic prosperity depends on entrepreneurs’ willingness to take risks, innovate, and invest. He stressed that states and nations that had achieved real prosperity did so by moving beyond resource abundance to building human capital and productive enterprises that create jobs and value. He noted that Oyo State’s economic transformation agenda was anchored on supporting entrepreneurs and private sector-led industrialisation as a pathway to shared prosperity. The governor assured investors of his administration’s continued support through enhanced security, investment facilitation, and other measures aimed at promoting business expansion and economic growth. He urged stakeholders to recognise the critical role of private businesses in creating economic opportunities, generating employment, and strengthening local industries. Makinde, who described the inauguration as a celebration of entrepreneurship, congratulated the company on building a thriving business conglomerate, comprising about 20 companies. He added that having the conglomerate’s headquarters in Ibadan would further reinforce the city’s position as a leading business hub and investment destination. He also expressed the state’s confidence in competing favourably with Lagos in attracting investments and hosting major business operations. He assured investors that his administration remained committed to supporting businesses to grow and expand, describing a thriving private sector as key to the state’s economic future.
